sentences.text: Austin Tice filed high-profile news reports during the Syrian civil war US journalist Austin Tice, who disappeared in Syria in 2012, was kidnapped in a calculated operation which was more than a month in the planning, the BBC can reveal.

sentences.text: A member of the group which detained Tice has also claimed the abduction was sanctioned by Syria's leader at the time, President Bashar al-Assad.

sentences.text: Tice was seen getting into a car with a driver he knew and trusted.

sentences.text: For years, many assumed they had stumbled upon a government checkpoint, and that the abduction of the journalist had been opportunistic.

sentences.text: But we have uncovered evidence that, in fact, his disappearance was anything but chance.

sentences.text: Series 3 of I'm Not A Monster Presents , we reveal the findings of a years-long investigation into what happened to Tice, who had been reporting on Syria's civil war at the time.

sentences.text: His case has been followed closely by international media and cited by successive US presidents.

sentences.text: Josh Baker enters a dangerous world of fear, greed and betrayal as he uncovers what happened in one of the biggest missing-person cases of our time - the abduction of Austin Tice.

sentences.text: Georgetown University law student Tice, who had served as a US Marines captain, was last seen in a video - blindfolded and in apparent distress - posted more than a month after his capture.

sentences.text: As the regime fell 12 years later, tens of thousands of people emerged from the administration's prisons.

sentences.text: Tice was not one of them.

sentences.text: We obtained co-ordinates from an intelligence source for multiple locations US authorities suspected he could have been held at, and searched for him for more than a month, but found no sign of him.

sentences.text: A former Syrian commander has said Tice was executed .

sentences.text: Others have questioned this account and no remains have been found.

sentences.text: But in the aftermath of the regime's collapse, we did uncover secret Syrian intelligence files on Tice - hundreds of pages of internal records providing the first definitive proof that it was the regime that had held the journalist.

sentences.text: Two crucial questions remained unanswered, however: how exactly had Tice been taken in the first place?

sentences.text: And, who was responsible for his abduction?

sentences.text: We have spoken to a number of men from the regime involved in Tice's detention, and have reviewed recordings of discussions about it.
sentences.article_title: Assad regime planned US journalist Austin Tice's kidnap for weeks, BBC finds

sentences.text: One man we spoke to, Abu Ali, is a former member of the National Defence Forces (NDF), a militia which was fiercely loyal to Assad.

sentences.text: He says the abduction operation began when Tice's driver - who multiple sources say had been passing the regime information for some time - told a senior NDF member that Tice was moving through rebel-held areas, reporting on the opposition.

sentences.text: Tice had pushed into areas most journalists deemed too dangerous and was writing front-page stories for the Washington Post.

sentences.text: The Assad regime was cracking down on anyone highlighting its human rights abuses.

sentences.text: We have been told the NDF member Tice's driver spoke to was Sakr Rustom - not just any NDF militia contact, but nephew of Bassam al-Hassan, one of Assad's most trusted security figures and head of the NDF.

sentences.text: "Bring him to us," Assad replied, claims Abu Ali.

sentences.text: Gary Summerfield told his family "this lady needs one of my kidneys more than I need two of them" A woman who shared a desperate plea for a kidney on Facebook has undergone a lifesaving transplant after a stranger offered to be her donor.

sentences.text: Norman Goodman underwent controversial electric shock therapy More victims of controversial electric shock therapy used to try to change their sexuality have come forward to call on the government to investigate the historical "scandal".
sentences.article_title: 'I was given electric shocks to knock the homosexuality out of my brain'

sentences.text: They spoke out after the BBC revealed that more than 260 people had been subjected to the discredited treatment at NHS hospitals in the 1960s and 1970s.
sentences.article_title: 'I was given electric shocks to knock the homosexuality out of my brain'

sentences.text: The people, who are now in their 70s and 80s, said they had been left physically and emotionally traumatised by their experiences.
sentences.article_title: 'I was given electric shocks to knock the homosexuality out of my brain'

sentences.text: And while the government said it would be drafting legislation to ban "aversion therapy", ten months on, the people spoken to by the BBC said they were still yet to receive an apology for what they had endured.
sentences.article_title: 'I was given electric shocks to knock the homosexuality out of my brain'

sentences.text: The BBC's investigation uncovered evidence that LGBT+ patients were subjected to electric shock aversion therapy in NHS hospitals across England.
sentences.article_title: 'I was given electric shocks to knock the homosexuality out of my brain'

sentences.text: Patients were shown images associated with same-sex attraction while being given painful electric shocks in an attempt to change their sexuality.
sentences.article_title: 'I was given electric shocks to knock the homosexuality out of my brain'

sentences.text: Norman came forward following an earlier BBC investigation into electric shock therapy Norman Goodman, 75, said that from childhood he felt more like a girl than a boy, and told his parents that he wanted to be female.
sentences.article_title: 'I was given electric shocks to knock the homosexuality out of my brain'

sentences.text: He was admitted to a psychiatric hospital in Manchester when he was 18, in the late 1960s.
sentences.article_title: 'I was given electric shocks to knock the homosexuality out of my brain'

sentences.text: He told the BBC doctors said they would try to make it easier for him, but he was given electric shocks.
sentences.article_title: 'I was given electric shocks to knock the homosexuality out of my brain'

sentences.text: "I didn't realise it was to knock the homosexuality out of my brain," he told the BBC.
sentences.article_title: 'I was given electric shocks to knock the homosexuality out of my brain'

sentences.text: He said he was strapped to a bed and electrodes were put on his arms, legs and on either side of his head, before electricity was passed through them.

sentences.text: " It was absolutely terrible.

sentences.text: They started shocking me.
sentences.article_title: 'I was given electric shocks to knock the homosexuality out of my brain'

sentences.text: "And next thing I knew, it was as though I didn't know where I was.
sentences.article_title: 'I was given electric shocks to knock the homosexuality out of my brain'

sentences.text: "I didn't even know who I was.
sentences.article_title: 'I was given electric shocks to knock the homosexuality out of my brain'

sentences.text: I had no appetite and no energy.

sentences.article_title: 'I was given electric shocks to knock the homosexuality out of my brain'

sentences.article_title: How being music's Mr Nice Guy contributed to biggest crisis of Ed Sheeran's career

sentences.article_title: How being music's Mr Nice Guy contributed to biggest crisis of Ed Sheeran's career

sentences.article_title: How being music's Mr Nice Guy contributed to biggest crisis of Ed Sheeran's career

sentences.article_title: How being music's Mr Nice Guy contributed to biggest crisis of Ed Sheeran's career

sentences.text: But like most artists, he leans left.

sentences.article_title: Eleanor Donaldson case prompts Stormont review of trials of the facts

sentences.text: The ministers will appoint an external reviewer with the review aiming to launch in late October and conclude by the end of February 2027.
sentences.article_title: Eleanor Donaldson case prompts Stormont review of trials of the facts

sentences.text: The letter to Stormont's justice committee said the move came in the wake of "public concern and interest" on trials of the facts, and that work would now take place on the terms of reference of the review.

sentences.text: Both the Department of Justice and the Department of Health have been contacted for comment.

sentences.text: A trial of the facts is an option that is open to prosecutors if a court determines that a person is unfit to stand trial and criminal proceedings cannot go ahead.
sentences.article_title: Eleanor Donaldson case prompts Stormont review of trials of the facts

sentences.text: It takes the place of a criminal trial and is used to determine whether an accused committed the acts alleged.
sentences.article_title: Eleanor Donaldson case prompts Stormont review of trials of the facts

sentences.text: It cannot result in a conviction, but if the court is not satisfied that the accused committed the acts alleged, then he/she will be acquitted.
sentences.article_title: Eleanor Donaldson case prompts Stormont review of trials of the facts

sentences.text: The procedure is allowed for in legislation by Article 49A of the Mental Health (Northern Ireland) Order 1986.
sentences.article_title: Eleanor Donaldson case prompts Stormont review of trials of the facts

sentences.text: The mechanism is not used often but one high-profile example was in the trial of former IRA leader Ivor Bell in 2019.
sentences.article_title: Eleanor Donaldson case prompts Stormont review of trials of the facts

sentences.text: In some ways, it is similar to a normal criminal trial - the prosecution puts its evidence against the defendant before a judge and jury in a courtroom.
sentences.article_title: Eleanor Donaldson case prompts Stormont review of trials of the facts

sentences.text: However, perhaps the key difference, is that the accused does not play a part in proceedings, and does not even need to be in court.
sentences.article_title: Eleanor Donaldson case prompts Stormont review of trials of the facts

sentences.text: That was the case with Eleanor Donaldson, who was not present on any day of the four-week trial in which evidence was heard against her and her husband.
sentences.article_title: Eleanor Donaldson case prompts Stormont review of trials of the facts

sentences.text: However, in a trial of the facts the accused will be represented by a legal team and their lawyers can question the witnesses, challenge the evidence and make legal submissions on their behalf.
sentences.article_title: Eleanor Donaldson case prompts Stormont review of trials of the facts

sentences.text: Ian Turkington KC represented Eleanor Donaldson during her trial of the facts, cross-examining witnesses and issuing closing remarks on behalf of his client towards the end of the trial.
sentences.article_title: Eleanor Donaldson case prompts Stormont review of trials of the facts

sentences.text: Then there is the major differences in what the outcome can be in a trial of the facts.
sentences.article_title: Eleanor Donaldson case prompts Stormont review of trials of the facts

sentences.text: Instead of being asked to return a verdict of guilty or not guilty, the jury are asked to decide whether or not the accused committed the offence with which they were charged.
sentences.article_title: Eleanor Donaldson case prompts Stormont review of trials of the facts

sentences.text: The focus is on what they are alleged to have physically done - not their state of mind at the time.
sentences.article_title: Eleanor Donaldson case prompts Stormont review of trials of the facts

sentences.text: In a normal criminal trial, a jury would be invited to decide whether or not a defendant had the mental faculties required to be guilty of the offence as well.
sentences.article_title: Eleanor Donaldson case prompts Stormont review of trials of the facts

sentences.text: The standard of proof remains the same - a jury must be sure beyond all reasonable doubt that the accused committed the acts alleged.
sentences.article_title: Eleanor Donaldson case prompts Stormont review of trials of the facts

sentences.text: The accused cannot be convicted but they can be acquitted if the jury decide they didn't commit the acts alleged.
sentences.article_title: Eleanor Donaldson case prompts Stormont review of trials of the facts

sentences.text: Speaking to BBC Radio Ulster's Good Morning Ulster programme, solicitor Paul Dougan described a trial of the facts as a "fusion between criminal justice and mental health provision".
sentences.article_title: Eleanor Donaldson case prompts Stormont review of trials of the facts

sentences.text: He said there is a "relatively high bar" with regards to medical evidence that needs to be presented, which requires oral evidence from a medical practitioner and a report from at least one further medical practitioner.
sentences.article_title: Eleanor Donaldson case prompts Stormont review of trials of the facts

sentences.text: He added that people may feel a trial of the facts is "some form of lesser process" for someone who was medically unfit, which he would "argue against".
sentences.article_title: Eleanor Donaldson case prompts Stormont review of trials of the facts

sentences.text: "With the involvement of medical practitioners and the interrogation of that process by a judge, at the moment it seems to me that the process is quite robust and a very high evidential threshold to be overcome.
sentences.article_title: Eleanor Donaldson case prompts Stormont review of trials of the facts

sentences.text: "I would just caution people against jumping to conclusions based on a particularly high profile case that has brought these issue to the fore," Dougan said.

sentences.text: A series of social media adverts for AI apps have been banned by a UK watchdog for promoting "the creation of sexually explicit content and objectification of women".
sentences.article_title: AI app ads promoting 'objectification of women' banned by watchdog

sentences.text: The Advertising Standards Authority (ASA) said five ads uploaded to Meta platforms for AI companion and video generating apps had objectified and sexualised women, including through harmful gender stereotypes.
sentences.article_title: AI app ads promoting 'objectification of women' banned by watchdog

sentences.text: One of the ads used sexualised images of a girl under 18 to promote an AI companion app - while others invited users to upload images of their "crush" and turn images into "sizzling" videos.
sentences.article_title: AI app ads promoting 'objectification of women' banned by watchdog

sentences.text: Meta had already removed the offending ads.
sentences.article_title: AI app ads promoting 'objectification of women' banned by watchdog

sentences.text: But Nicky Baker of the ASA said such content had the potential "to cause real-world harm".
sentences.article_title: AI app ads promoting 'objectification of women' banned by watchdog

sentences.text: "We take a firm line on ads that are likely to cause serious or widespread offence and these ads are a clear example of why that matters," she said.
sentences.article_title: AI app ads promoting 'objectification of women' banned by watchdog

sentences.text: "Encouraging and condoning the objectification of women and the creation of explicit content from people's images has the potential to cause real-world harm." The ASA also said many of the ads it banned had promoted the creation of sexually explicit content using real women's images without their consent.
sentences.article_title: AI app ads promoting 'objectification of women' banned by watchdog

sentences.text: It comes only months after the UK outlawed apps to create non-consensual deepfake nude imagery - sparked by outrage over X's chatbot Grok complying with requests to nudify images of women on the platform .
sentences.article_title: AI app ads promoting 'objectification of women' banned by watchdog

sentences.text: The ASA said the law had changed during its investigations and that ads identified in future would be considered in light of both the law and its own rules.
sentences.article_title: AI app ads promoting 'objectification of women' banned by watchdog

sentences.text: Where ads are identified as illegal, it said it may notify platforms and law enforcement.
sentences.article_title: AI app ads promoting 'objectification of women' banned by watchdog

sentences.text: The ads were identified by the regulator using its AI-powered "Active Ad Monitoring System", which proactively searches for ads which might violate UK rules.
sentences.article_title: AI app ads promoting 'objectification of women' banned by watchdog

sentences.text: It said the five ads it were banned had depicted women irresponsibly, and were likely to cause serious or widespread offence.
sentences.article_title: AI app ads promoting 'objectification of women' banned by watchdog

sentences.text: One ad for an AI companion generator, developed by Animcha Ltd, was also found to have portrayed someone under 18 in a sexual way, the ASA said.
sentences.article_title: AI app ads promoting 'objectification of women' banned by watchdog

sentences.text: It presented the synthetic female character as someone users could "customise" and instruct, combining sexualised imagery with childlike clothing and objects.
sentences.article_title: AI app ads promoting 'objectification of women' banned by watchdog

sentences.article_title: AI app ads promoting 'objectification of women' banned by watchdog

sentences.article_title: AI app ads promoting 'objectification of women' banned by watchdog

sentences.text: Further adverts for image generation tool Rusto AI, which encouraged users to create sexualised videos from photographs, were found to have condoned the digital manipulation of women's images to create sexually explicit content.
sentences.article_title: AI app ads promoting 'objectification of women' banned by watchdog

sentences.text: And an ad for an AI image-to-video generation app PictoPop used sexualised imagery to demonstrate the tool, including by portraying the woman in a submissive position.

sentences.text: The state pension is expected to top £13,000 a year, reigniting the debate about its long-term affordability and generational fairness.

sentences.text: The so-called triple lock pension policy guarantees that the state pension will increase by either average wage growth, inflation or 2.5% - whichever is highest.

sentences.article_title: Can Europe recharge its battery industry?

sentences.text: The government has introduced a bill to end antiquated laws preventing Roman Catholic or Jewish prime ministers from being involved in the process of making Church of England appointments.
sentences.article_title: Government to end ban on Catholic and Jewish PMs' involvement in Church appointments

sentences.text: It was among the first pieces of legislation to be introduced to Parliament under Prime Minister Andy Burnham, himself a Catholic, who has called the current laws "unacceptable".
sentences.article_title: Government to end ban on Catholic and Jewish PMs' involvement in Church appointments

sentences.text: When appointing bishops and archbishops, the Church presents a candidate to the prime minister who then advises the monarch on who to install in the role.
sentences.article_title: Government to end ban on Catholic and Jewish PMs' involvement in Church appointments

sentences.text: Although the involvement of the prime minister in this process has become more of a formality in recent years, legislation still exists that specifically bars Roman Catholics and Jews from exercising this responsibility.
sentences.article_title: Government to end ban on Catholic and Jewish PMs' involvement in Church appointments

sentences.text: That is why earlier this month Burnham, the first Catholic prime minister, transferred the responsibility of advising the King on Church appointments to the Lord Chancellor.
sentences.article_title: Government to end ban on Catholic and Jewish PMs' involvement in Church appointments

sentences.text: But the prime minster said it was "unacceptable for there to be a legislative bar against people of any faith performing all the functions of my office".
sentences.article_title: Government to end ban on Catholic and Jewish PMs' involvement in Church appointments

sentences.text: The Roman Catholic Relief Act 1829 and the Jews Relief Act 1858 are the existing laws in question.
sentences.article_title: Government to end ban on Catholic and Jewish PMs' involvement in Church appointments

sentences.text: When those laws were introduced, they actually eased some of the restrictions on Catholics' and Jews' participation in public life.
sentences.article_title: Government to end ban on Catholic and Jewish PMs' involvement in Church appointments

sentences.text: This included what was, in effect, a prohibition on them becoming MPs.
sentences.article_title: Government to end ban on Catholic and Jewish PMs' involvement in Church appointments

sentences.text: But the law still stipulated that prime ministers of those faiths could not be involved - "directly or indirectly" - in advising during the process of making Church appointments.
sentences.article_title: Government to end ban on Catholic and Jewish PMs' involvement in Church appointments

sentences.text: The law relating to Jews contains a similar threat.
sentences.article_title: Government to end ban on Catholic and Jewish PMs' involvement in Church appointments

sentences.text: These laws and restrictions remain in effect.
sentences.article_title: Government to end ban on Catholic and Jewish PMs' involvement in Church appointments

sentences.text: That is partly because, until now, they have had no practical effect - before Burnham, there has not been a Catholic or Jewish prime minister.

sentences.text: Although Benjamin Disraeli - prime minister in the late-1800s - was born to a Jewish family, his father renounced Judaism and had his children baptised into the Church of England.
sentences.article_title: Government to end ban on Catholic and Jewish PMs' involvement in Church appointments

sentences.text: Another former Prime Minister, Tony Blair, is a Roman Catholic, but his conversion formally took place six months after he stepped down.
sentences.article_title: Government to end ban on Catholic and Jewish PMs' involvement in Church appointments

sentences.text: Some prime ministers have taken a more interventionist approach.
sentences.article_title: Government to end ban on Catholic and Jewish PMs' involvement in Church appointments

sentences.article_title: Government to end ban on Catholic and Jewish PMs' involvement in Church appointments

sentences.text: Although the archaic laws preventing Jews and Roman Catholics advising on Church appointments technically relates to the Church of Scotland too, in reality the appointment of elders and ministers within the Church of Scotland no longer has any outside involvement.

sentences.text: A former top civil servant received a record pay-off of nearly £860,000 after he was forced out of his job by Sir Keir Starmer, just 14 months after the then-prime minister appointed him.
sentences.article_title: Former top civil servant received pay-off of nearly £860,000

sentences.text: Lord Wormald left his role as cabinet secretary and head of the Civil Service in February by "mutual agreement" following months of media reports suggesting Downing Street was unhappy with his performance.
sentences.article_title: Former top civil servant received pay-off of nearly £860,000

sentences.text: The Cabinet Office's accounts , external show there was "contractual compensation" of £332,897 and "additional severance" of £526,598.
sentences.article_title: Former top civil servant received pay-off of nearly £860,000

sentences.text: The BBC understands the size of the pay-off was partly to cover Lord Wormald's pension contributions as his removal from office essentially cut his civil service career short.
sentences.article_title: Former top civil servant received pay-off of nearly £860,000

sentences.text: He also was compensated for a mandatory "waiting period" following his departure from government.
sentences.article_title: Former top civil servant received pay-off of nearly £860,000

sentences.text: As cabinet secretary he would have had regular access to sensitive information about national security, foreign policy and the UK economy.
sentences.article_title: Former top civil servant received pay-off of nearly £860,000

sentences.text: His salary for the period 1 April 2025 to 13 February was between £210,000 and £215,000, according to the accounts, bringing his total for the year to more than £1m.
sentences.article_title: Former top civil servant received pay-off of nearly £860,000

sentences.text: A Cabinet Office spokesperson said: "We do not comment on HR matters.
sentences.article_title: Former top civil servant received pay-off of nearly £860,000

sentences.text: "The permanent secretary at the Cabinet Office received a ministerial direction from the then-prime minister to proceed with the payment to the former cabinet secretary.
sentences.article_title: Former top civil servant received pay-off of nearly £860,000

sentences.text: Their exchange of letters is a matter of public record." The accounts state Sir Keir authorised the "special severance package" on 16 February.
sentences.article_title: Former top civil servant received pay-off of nearly £860,000

sentences.text: A note in them also states: "The former cabinet secretary elected to take early payment of his pension.
sentences.article_title: Former top civil servant received pay-off of nearly £860,000

sentences.text: "The majority of the total severance payment was used to ensure he could access the full value of his pension that would have been due at normal retirement age, rather than it being reduced for early payment." The BBC has approached Lord Wormald and Sir Keir for comment.
sentences.article_title: Former top civil servant received pay-off of nearly £860,000

sentences.text: Conservative shadow Cabinet Office minister Alex Burghart said: "Chris Wormald was just one of many civil servants and advisers fired by Keir Starmer as he tried to save his own skin.
sentences.article_title: Former top civil servant received pay-off of nearly £860,000

sentences.text: "This payout is another appalling waste of taxpayers' money by Labour." The UK's top civil servant sits next to the prime minister during cabinet minister meetings, which usually take place weekly in Downing Street when Parliament is sitting.
sentences.article_title: Former top civil servant received pay-off of nearly £860,000

sentences.article_title: Former top civil servant received pay-off of nearly £860,000

sentences.article_title: Former top civil servant received pay-off of nearly £860,000

sentences.text: As a career civil servant, some questioned whether he was the best person to reform the Civil Service.
sentences.article_title: Former top civil servant received pay-off of nearly £860,000

sentences.article_title: Former top civil servant received pay-off of nearly £860,000

sentences.text: Lord Wormald was replaced by Dame Antonia Romeo .

sentences.text: Villagers in Piddington have voted on whether the village should leave the UK Voters in a small village headed to the polls for an independence vote over government plans to house asylum seekers at a nearby former Ministry of Defence (MoD) site.
sentences.article_title: Villagers vote on independence over asylum plans

sentences.text: The residents of Piddington, in Oxfordshire, voted over Home Office proposals to house up to 1,256 male asylum seekers at MoD Bicester .
sentences.article_title: Villagers vote on independence over asylum plans

sentences.text: The symbolic referendum on whether to leave the UK has been organised by the local parish council, with polling taking place between 07:00 and 19:00 BST.
sentences.article_title: Villagers vote on independence over asylum plans

sentences.text: Ahead of the vote, council chair Tim McNally said the government "does not want to engage with villagers concerns".
sentences.article_title: Villagers vote on independence over asylum plans

sentences.text: "They actually have played every possible trick in the book to avoid engagement," he said.
sentences.article_title: Villagers vote on independence over asylum plans

sentences.text: They said the government was "engaging with local authorities to reduce the impact on communities and we've saved taxpayers more than £1bn on asylum support costs since the election".
sentences.article_title: Villagers vote on independence over asylum plans

sentences.text: "The Home Office has submitted an application to obtain planning permission to use the Bicester site for asylum accommodation, but it remains the case that no final decision has been taken on the site's future use," the spokesperson added.
sentences.article_title: Villagers vote on independence over asylum plans

sentences.text: Having just cast his vote, Herbert Owen said the referendum was not "just about Piddington".
sentences.article_title: Villagers vote on independence over asylum plans

sentences.text: "It means everything our grandparents, our parents fought for – today is the Battle of Britain," he said.
sentences.article_title: Villagers vote on independence over asylum plans

sentences.text: His wife, Jennifer Owen, said: "We can't actually leave the United Kingdom, but it just brings things out in the open more for the country as a whole." She added that the proposals would "change our lives forever" if it were to go ahead.
sentences.article_title: Villagers vote on independence over asylum plans

sentences.text: The government plans to provide accommodation for up to 1,256 men at the site near Bicester The Home Office first announced its plans for MoD Bicester in June.
sentences.article_title: Villagers vote on independence over asylum plans

sentences.text: "We are working to fairly house asylum seekers across the country, moving asylum seekers into alternative accommodation," a spokesperson said.
sentences.article_title: Villagers vote on independence over asylum plans

sentences.article_title: Villagers vote on independence over asylum plans

sentences.text: But that is not how many people in Piddington see the proposals , with 96% of voters supporting a referendum on independence from the UK in a vote held on 4 July - a date synonymous with another declaration of independence from the British state.
sentences.article_title: Villagers vote on independence over asylum plans

sentences.text: Last week, ahead of Tuesday's vote, 133 women from the village wrote to every female Member of Parliament saying "life as we know it will be destroyed" if the plans succeed.

sentences.text: Lord Blunkett spoke at a countryside campaigning event in central London An inheritance tax for farms was "a mistake" and Andy Burnham should use his premiership to listen to the countryside more, his longtime mentor Lord Blunkett has said.
sentences.article_title: Farm tax a mistake, Lord Blunkett says in call for Burnham 'rural reset'

sentences.text: The former Labour minister hit out at "Treasury economic orthodoxy" over the 20% tax on inherited agricultural assets worth more than £2.5m that came into force in April, ending a waiver farms had since the 1980s.
sentences.article_title: Farm tax a mistake, Lord Blunkett says in call for Burnham 'rural reset'

sentences.text: He spoke at the launch of a new campaign by the Countryside Alliance for a "rural reset" to reverse what the group says is a current set of policies "treating rural people as the enemy".
sentences.article_title: Farm tax a mistake, Lord Blunkett says in call for Burnham 'rural reset'

sentences.text: The government said it was "determined to rebuild trust" with farmers and that most estates were unaffected by the tax hike.
sentences.article_title: Farm tax a mistake, Lord Blunkett says in call for Burnham 'rural reset'

sentences.text: The tax, announced in last year's Budget under Sir Keir Starmer at half the 40% rate of standard inheritance tax, was initially proposed for inherited agricultural assets worth more than £1m.
sentences.article_title: Farm tax a mistake, Lord Blunkett says in call for Burnham 'rural reset'

sentences.text: A backlash led to it being watered down in December - to a raised threshold of £2.5m.
sentences.article_title: Farm tax a mistake, Lord Blunkett says in call for Burnham 'rural reset'

sentences.text: Some rural campaigners say this still impacts ordinary working family farms and are calling for it to be scrapped.
sentences.article_title: Farm tax a mistake, Lord Blunkett says in call for Burnham 'rural reset'

sentences.text: Burnham has not hinted any change or U-turn on the issue, but Lord Blunkett said he was confident the now-prime minister, who he hired as his parliamentary private secretary back in 2004, would get the message "very clearly and act accordingly".
sentences.article_title: Farm tax a mistake, Lord Blunkett says in call for Burnham 'rural reset'

sentences.text: "I think the family tax, the family farm imposition, was a mistake," the former Labour minister said, adding it "touched a nerve".
sentences.article_title: Farm tax a mistake, Lord Blunkett says in call for Burnham 'rural reset'

sentences.text: "It's very strange because we've never won so many rural seats since 1945 - around 135 Labour MPs are either rural or semi-rural - and their voices need to be heard much more clearly," he told the BBC.
sentences.article_title: Farm tax a mistake, Lord Blunkett says in call for Burnham 'rural reset'

sentences.text: Lord Blunkett also branded the government's planned ban on trail hunting a mistake, saying the practice was "doing no harm".
sentences.article_title: Farm tax a mistake, Lord Blunkett says in call for Burnham 'rural reset'

sentences.article_title: Farm tax a mistake, Lord Blunkett says in call for Burnham 'rural reset'

sentences.article_title: Farm tax a mistake, Lord Blunkett says in call for Burnham 'rural reset'

sentences.text: But it is worth setting out the law, in broad terms, now and how the government hopes to change it.

sentences.text: Right now, there is no limit on how much anyone, living in the UK or abroad, can give to a British political party as long as the individual is registered to vote in the UK.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Row over Reform's mega donations has mileage in it yet

sentences.text: But the government has been planning a change in the law for months, which would limit donations from Brits abroad to £100,000 each per year, backdated to 25 March this year.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Row over Reform's mega donations has mileage in it yet

sentences.text: But, crucially, the law hasn't changed yet and some of the key details in that proposed new law - such as what residency requirements would need to be passed to be classified as no longer being abroad - haven't been decided yet.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Row over Reform's mega donations has mileage in it yet

sentences.text: The reason for that date, 25 March, ministers argue, is that is the day a review by the retired civil servant Philip Rycroft was published, , external the first recommendation of which was that there should be "an annual cap on political donations from British voters living abroad".
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Row over Reform's mega donations has mileage in it yet

sentences.text: On that same day, the then-cabinet minister Steve Reed told the Commons , external that cap would be £100,000 per year.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Row over Reform's mega donations has mileage in it yet

sentences.text: He also added that it would "apply retrospectively" from that date onwards, even though the law at the time, and indeed now, has not yet changed.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Row over Reform's mega donations has mileage in it yet

sentences.text: Two big questions arise from this plan: is it proportionate to limit what British folk abroad can donate to UK political parties, given they are arguably less invested in the country than people living here?

sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Row over Reform's mega donations has mileage in it yet

sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Row over Reform's mega donations has mileage in it yet

sentences.text: Oregon was one of the first places in the world to offer help to die for some patients, in 1997, and so has nearly 30 years' experience.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: It has become the model on which other US assisted dying laws have been framed.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: In Oregon, assisted dying is open to terminally ill , external , mentally competent adults expected to die within six months - and must be signed off by two doctors.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: Since 1997 , external , 5,520 people have received a prescription for a lethal dose of medication - with 3,691 deaths.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: In a 2025 report , external , 61% of patients who ask for help to die had cancer, 14% had a neurological condition like motor neurone disease and 11% had heart disease.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: Around one in three of those prescribed a lethal dose don’t go ahead with it.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: Oregon is important for supporters of assisted dying in England and Wales as they point out it has remained restricted to terminally ill adults since its introduction.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: However, opponents say some of the rules have been relaxed.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: A residency requirement has been lifted, which means it is open to people from outside the state.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: The number of assisted deaths has also risen substantially over the years.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: Canada is the country often cited by opponents of assisted dying as an example of the so-called "slippery slope" - a place where assisted dying has been extended and made available to more people since it was first brought in.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: Medical assistance in dying (Maid) , external was introduced in 2016, initially just for the terminally ill.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: This was amended in 2021 and extended to those experiencing "unbearable suffering" from an irreversible illness or disability.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: It had been due to be extended to people with a mental illness but that is now on hold.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: Critics say the more the law is widened, the more disabled and vulnerable people will be put at risk.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: There has also been a dramatic growth in the number of people using Maid.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: Roughly one in every 20 deaths in Canada are now medically assisted , external , compared to about one in 100 in Oregon.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: Across Europe, several countries have legalised assisted dying: Switzerland, the Netherlands, Belgium, Luxembourg, Spain, Austria, Portugal and, most recently, France.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: Eligibility criteria vary widely.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: Some jurisdictions allow assisted dying for people who are not terminally ill, while others, including France, restrict it to adults with serious incurable illnesses nearing the end of life.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: Portugal's law was approved in 2023 but is not yet in force because of court and regulatory delays.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: In 2025, Tuscany became the first region of Italy to establish a legal process for medically assisted suicide.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: Earlier rulings by the constitutional courts in both Italy and Germany removed criminal penalties for assisted suicide in certain circumstances.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: The Netherlands and Belgium both legalised assisted dying more than 20 years ago for patients experiencing unbearable suffering from an incurable illness, including mental health issues.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: It has since been extended to children - the only European countries to allow this.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: Both allow euthanasia - or physician-assisted dying.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: Spain and Austria legalised assisted dying for both terminal illness and intolerable suffering in 2021 and 2022, respectively.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: In Austria, the drugs must be self-administered, whereas in Spain a medical professional can administer them.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: In England, Wales and Scotland, parliament has so far rejected assisted dying proposals.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: But assisted dying has already been legalised in one part of the British Isles.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: In July, Royal Assent was given to a bill in Jersey.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: Unlike at Westminster and Holyrood, the legislation was introduced by the Jersey government, which says it will take about 18 months to set up the service.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: The first assisted death could happen late next year.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: There will be a residency requirement of one year, in a bid to prevent so-called 'death tourism'.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: The measure, which most sets apart the Jersey legislation from the rest of the British Isles, concerns the manner in which those eligible for an assisted death can end their lives.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: Individuals will be able to choose to have a doctor administer a lethal dose intravenously, as happens in Spain, Canada, New Zealand and most of Australia.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: This is, in effect, voluntary euthanasia.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: It has become the preferred method of assisted dying in jurisdictions which allow this choice.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: The laws proposed at Westminster, Holyrood and Tynwald - Isle of Man - all state that death must be by self-administration, which usually means the individual swallowing a lethal dose.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: The Isle of Man assisted dying bill was passed by Tynwald (the Manx parliament) in March last year.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: As a UK Crown Dependency - like Jersey - it could not become law until granted Royal Assent.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: This was declined earlier this year by the UK Ministry of Justice, but Tynwald has since passed an updated bill which has been sent back to the UK government for a second time.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: If Royal Assent is granted, the Isle of Man expects the service to be operational next year.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: There is a residency requirement of five years.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: In the past few years voluntary assisted dying has become legal across most of Australia.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: Last month, the Northern Territory parliament became the last part of Australia to pass Voluntary Assisted Dying legislation.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: In New Zealand, patients must be terminally ill and expected to die within six months.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: That is extended to 12 months for those with a neurodegenerative condition in much of Australia.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: In both countries, patients can self-administer the lethal medication.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: But it can also be administered by a doctor or nurse, usually via an intravenous injection.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: In South America, Uruguay passed a law in 2025 to permit assisted dying for adults with an incurable or terminal illness.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: Across Latin America, Colombia, Ecuador and Cuba have decriminalised euthanasia.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: Additional reporting by Anthony Reuben and Gerry Georgieva
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: This video can not be played Watch: Former consultant hopes Letby inquiry recommendations will prevent deaths happening again One of the senior doctors who tried to raise concerns about Lucy Letby with hospital managers has told the BBC the final inquiry report makes for "grim reading".
sentences.article_title: Letby doctor says inquiry 'grim reading' and he wishes 'we had been brave enough to follow suspicions'

sentences.text: Consultant paediatrician Dr John Gibbs worked at the Countess of Chester Hospital throughout the period in 2015 to 2016 when Letby murdered seven babies, and attempted to murder seven more, on the neonatal unit.
sentences.article_title: Letby doctor says inquiry 'grim reading' and he wishes 'we had been brave enough to follow suspicions'

sentences.text: He said that he accepted that consultants must bear "collective" responsibility for some of the failings identified in the report.
sentences.article_title: Letby doctor says inquiry 'grim reading' and he wishes 'we had been brave enough to follow suspicions'

sentences.text: "I wish we consultants had been brave enough to follow our suspicions and escalate things to the police earlier," he told the BBC.
sentences.article_title: Letby doctor says inquiry 'grim reading' and he wishes 'we had been brave enough to follow suspicions'

sentences.text: "When I say, 'we consultants', I am responsible as well and if my other consultant colleagues didn't go to the police, I should have." The Thirlwall Inquiry was launched after former nurse Letby was convicted in 2023, and the final report was published on Tuesday.
sentences.article_title: Letby doctor says inquiry 'grim reading' and he wishes 'we had been brave enough to follow suspicions'

sentences.text: In the 822-page document, Lady Justice Thirlwall described "a complete failure to protect babies on the neonatal unit at the Countess of Chester Hospital".
sentences.article_title: Letby doctor says inquiry 'grim reading' and he wishes 'we had been brave enough to follow suspicions'

sentences.text: The report found that the police "should have been notified earlier than they were" and that hospital managers had repeatedly dismissed consultants' concerns.
sentences.article_title: Letby doctor says inquiry 'grim reading' and he wishes 'we had been brave enough to follow suspicions'

sentences.text: Reflecting on the findings for the first time, Gibbs said: "I wasn't expecting it to be an easy read and it certainly isn't.
sentences.article_title: Letby doctor says inquiry 'grim reading' and he wishes 'we had been brave enough to follow suspicions'

sentences.text: I'd imagine it's an extremely difficult read for the parents of the babies concerned.
sentences.article_title: Letby doctor says inquiry 'grim reading' and he wishes 'we had been brave enough to follow suspicions'

sentences.text: "But it was during that 11 months after Lucy Letby was moved off the unit, before the police got involved, that it was a very difficult atmosphere, very tense, very stressful dealing with the managers," he added.
sentences.article_title: Letby doctor says inquiry 'grim reading' and he wishes 'we had been brave enough to follow suspicions'

sentences.text: Managers "were determined to ensure that we accepted Lucy Letby had been wrongly suspected of doing any harm," the senior doctor explained.
sentences.article_title: Letby doctor says inquiry 'grim reading' and he wishes 'we had been brave enough to follow suspicions'

sentences.text: He also spoke of the failures of his and his wider team, specifically referencing a doctor who disregarded blood test results that suggested a baby had been poisoned with insulin in August 2015.
sentences.article_title: Letby doctor says inquiry 'grim reading' and he wishes 'we had been brave enough to follow suspicions'

sentences.text: While one of his colleagues had missed the relevance of the results when they came back from the lab, it had been a collective team failure, Dr Gibbs concluded.
sentences.article_title: Letby doctor says inquiry 'grim reading' and he wishes 'we had been brave enough to follow suspicions'

sentences.text: "Others of us were on call and covering the neonatal unit over the next week or two before the baby moved out of the unit.
sentences.article_title: Letby doctor says inquiry 'grim reading' and he wishes 'we had been brave enough to follow suspicions'

sentences.text: We all had the opportunity to review the notes." Letby, who maintains her innocence, is serving 15 whole-life terms for the murders and has twice been denied permission to appeal against her convictions.
sentences.article_title: Letby doctor says inquiry 'grim reading' and he wishes 'we had been brave enough to follow suspicions'

sentences.text: The Criminal Cases Review Commission (CCRC), an independent body set up to examine potential miscarriages of justice, is currently reviewing her convictions.
sentences.article_title: Letby doctor says inquiry 'grim reading' and he wishes 'we had been brave enough to follow suspicions'

sentences.text: The inquiry looked into the actions of managers at the hospital where Lucy Letby worked In the weeks and months after Letby was convicted, questions about the case arose in the form of online conspiracy theories and discourse from serious academics, including medical experts and statisticians.
sentences.article_title: Letby doctor says inquiry 'grim reading' and he wishes 'we had been brave enough to follow suspicions'

sentences.text: Gibbs said that the continuing support for Letby had taken a toll on him and other consultants, and that claims she had been wrongly convicted were "frustrating and difficult" to hear.
sentences.article_title: Letby doctor says inquiry 'grim reading' and he wishes 'we had been brave enough to follow suspicions'

sentences.text: "I particularly find the misinformation that's on the internet is difficult to deal with," he said.
sentences.article_title: Letby doctor says inquiry 'grim reading' and he wishes 'we had been brave enough to follow suspicions'

sentences.text: He added: "I haven't changed my mind that I think Lucy Letby is guilty." However, he emphasised that, because of the "calibre of some of the people who've raised concerns", it is "important" that the evidence used to convict Letby is being examined by the CCRC.
sentences.article_title: Letby doctor says inquiry 'grim reading' and he wishes 'we had been brave enough to follow suspicions'

sentences.text: Thirlwall's report called for a series of urgent reforms to neonatal units, including CCTV for all cots and incubators, and restricting access to insulin.
sentences.article_title: Letby doctor says inquiry 'grim reading' and he wishes 'we had been brave enough to follow suspicions'

sentences.text: After the report was published, Health Secretary Yvette Cooper said officials will "urgently develop plans" to introduce live-streaming cameras on England's baby wards.
sentences.article_title: Letby doctor says inquiry 'grim reading' and he wishes 'we had been brave enough to follow suspicions'

sentences.text: Thirlwall said some of the babies Letby killed could have been saved if managers at the Countess of Chester Hospital had taken action earlier.
sentences.article_title: Letby doctor says inquiry 'grim reading' and he wishes 'we had been brave enough to follow suspicions'

sentences.text: Letby was moved on to administrative duties in July 2016 after consultants expressed concerns about her to the hospital's executive team.
sentences.article_title: Letby doctor says inquiry 'grim reading' and he wishes 'we had been brave enough to follow suspicions'

sentences.text: But the inquiry has found that alarm bells should have been sounded earlier.
sentences.article_title: Letby doctor says inquiry 'grim reading' and he wishes 'we had been brave enough to follow suspicions'

sentences.text: There were several "missed opportunities" for hospital bosses to intervene, the report said, including when three babies died in one cluster in June 2015.
sentences.article_title: Letby doctor says inquiry 'grim reading' and he wishes 'we had been brave enough to follow suspicions'

sentences.article_title: Letby doctor says inquiry 'grim reading' and he wishes 'we had been brave enough to follow suspicions'

sentences.text: Thirlwall described the lack of consideration shown to parents as "reprehensible".
sentences.article_title: Letby doctor says inquiry 'grim reading' and he wishes 'we had been brave enough to follow suspicions'

sentences.text: Nearly one in four people are thought to have bruxism, although most are unaware they grind their teeth Ella can't remember when she first started grinding her teeth at night, but she can vividly recall the excruciating jaw ache, the headaches, and being told her molars were disappearing.
sentences.article_title: Some dentists say more young people are grinding their teeth - are you one of them?

sentences.text: "I was in so much pain," Ella says.
sentences.article_title: Some dentists say more young people are grinding their teeth - are you one of them?

sentences.text: "My face was changing shape and my teeth were at risk of breaking - I knew I had to do something about it." The 31-year-old has bruxism, a condition which can cause regular and often intense teeth grinding, but says the treatment she's recently had has "without a doubt" changed her life.
sentences.article_title: Some dentists say more young people are grinding their teeth - are you one of them?

sentences.text: Bruxism affects millions like Ella across the UK , external .
sentences.article_title: Some dentists say more young people are grinding their teeth - are you one of them?

sentences.text: Some studies suggest nearly one in four people experience the condition, although many may be unaware until symptoms appear.
sentences.article_title: Some dentists say more young people are grinding their teeth - are you one of them?

sentences.text: According to the British Dental Association there is some anecdotal evidence that bruxism is becoming more common, but no specific figures.
sentences.article_title: Some dentists say more young people are grinding their teeth - are you one of them?

sentences.text: However, some dentists have told the BBC they are worried about the increasing number of young people they're seeing with dental problems caused by incessant gnashing.
sentences.article_title: Some dentists say more young people are grinding their teeth - are you one of them?

sentences.text: "It is definitely on the rise," Dr Aditi Desai, president of the British Society of Dental Sleep Medicine (BSDSM), says.
sentences.article_title: Some dentists say more young people are grinding their teeth - are you one of them?

sentences.text: And can it actually be a good thing in some cases?
sentences.article_title: Some dentists say more young people are grinding their teeth - are you one of them?

sentences.text: Bruxism is an umbrella term which groups together four different jaw movements - clenching, grinding, bracing and thrusting.
sentences.article_title: Some dentists say more young people are grinding their teeth - are you one of them?

sentences.text: Some people grind at night, others through the day.
sentences.article_title: Some dentists say more young people are grinding their teeth - are you one of them?

sentences.text: Some barely notice they're doing it, while others can gnash through mouthguards and wake even the deepest sleeping bed partners.
sentences.article_title: Some dentists say more young people are grinding their teeth - are you one of them?

sentences.text: So how can you tell if you do it?
sentences.article_title: Some dentists say more young people are grinding their teeth - are you one of them?

sentences.text: Psychotherapist Rahi Popat says more of his clients - particularly younger ones - say they or someone else have noticed they've been grinding their teeth, "and they can often link that to a really stressful time in their lives and realise that's when their teeth grinding either increased or even started".
sentences.article_title: Some dentists say more young people are grinding their teeth - are you one of them?

sentences.text: Trauma and stress can put you in "fight or flight" mode, where your heart rate increases, you release adrenaline, and your muscles tense, preparing the body for an external threat, he says.
sentences.article_title: Some dentists say more young people are grinding their teeth - are you one of them?

sentences.text: And because the jaw and the nervous system are so closely linked through the major cranial nerves, our muscles are triggered and we clench and grind our teeth.
sentences.article_title: Some dentists say more young people are grinding their teeth - are you one of them?

sentences.text: "If we do it overnight, it's a way of our bodies releasing some of the stress and tension we might have felt through the day," Popat explains.
sentences.article_title: Some dentists say more young people are grinding their teeth - are you one of them?

sentences.text: For Ella, nocturnal teeth grinding in her sleep became a way to release tension that had built up while she was awake.
sentences.article_title: Some dentists say more young people are grinding their teeth - are you one of them?

sentences.text: "I know it's to do with my stress levels," Ella says.
sentences.article_title: Some dentists say more young people are grinding their teeth - are you one of them?

sentences.text: "I have high functioning anxiety - you wouldn't think it if you met me.
sentences.article_title: Some dentists say more young people are grinding their teeth - are you one of them?

sentences.text: "I'm busy, and I go out a lot to mask it." In her 20s, she says she just "put up" with the pain.
sentences.article_title: Some dentists say more young people are grinding their teeth - are you one of them?

sentences.text: But a few years later, when her dentist told her that her teeth were at risk, Ella decided to get treatment.
sentences.article_title: Some dentists say more young people are grinding their teeth - are you one of them?

sentences.text: After her dentist injected her jaw muscles with Botox, Ella says her sleep and mental health improved Even though it's not routinely offered on the NHS, Ella decided to pay her dentist to inject Botox into her masseter muscles - the ones that control her jaw.
sentences.article_title: Some dentists say more young people are grinding their teeth - are you one of them?

sentences.text: The procedure relaxed them and reduced the tension in her face, and should last 3 to 4 months.
sentences.article_title: Some dentists say more young people are grinding their teeth - are you one of them?

sentences.text: "Over the past few months I've been able to sleep properly," she says.
sentences.article_title: Some dentists say more young people are grinding their teeth - are you one of them?

sentences.text: "I've got so much more energy in the mornings, the pain has reduced and my face is not as square." Dr Simon Cove, a dentist who treats both private and NHS patients, says the physical impact of grinding on our teeth can be huge.
sentences.article_title: Some dentists say more young people are grinding their teeth - are you one of them?

sentences.text: He uses a 3D scanner to assess his patients' teeth, and can see the wear over time.
sentences.article_title: Some dentists say more young people are grinding their teeth - are you one of them?

sentences.text: "Often people are not even aware they are doing it, but then we get to see the damage," he says.
sentences.article_title: Some dentists say more young people are grinding their teeth - are you one of them?

sentences.text: "If the teeth have been worn down to such an extent, treatment can be extremely complex and can cost thousands of pounds." But he says such cases are relatively uncommon and can take years to develop.
sentences.article_title: Some dentists say more young people are grinding their teeth - are you one of them?

sentences.text: A 3D scan can reveal the damage that teeth grinders are doing to their teeth While you can treat the symptoms - by wearing a mouthguard, for example - getting to the source of what's causing your teeth grinding is just as important, says dental sleep specialist, Dr Aditi Desai.
sentences.article_title: Some dentists say more young people are grinding their teeth - are you one of them?

sentences.text: "Too often," she says, "dentists give out mouthguards without checking why it is happening." It's vital that serious, underlying conditions like obstructive sleep apnoea (OSA) are considered, she says.
sentences.article_title: Some dentists say more young people are grinding their teeth - are you one of them?

sentences.text: OSA is caused by a blocked airway, so a patient may grind their teeth to move the blockage in order to be able to breathe again.
sentences.article_title: Some dentists say more young people are grinding their teeth - are you one of them?

sentences.text: "That's a very good example of why bruxism can keep you alive," says Prof Frank Lobbezoo, a leading researcher on the condition.
sentences.article_title: Some dentists say more young people are grinding their teeth - are you one of them?

sentences.text: And even though bruxism has its negatives (tooth damage, sleep disruption, jaw ache, to name but a few), it's not always the "bad guy", he explains.
sentences.article_title: Some dentists say more young people are grinding their teeth - are you one of them?

sentences.text: "Bruxism is also important for the production of saliva," Lobbezoo says.
sentences.article_title: Some dentists say more young people are grinding their teeth - are you one of them?

sentences.text: "Moving the jaw muscles activates the big salivary glands.
sentences.article_title: Some dentists say more young people are grinding their teeth - are you one of them?

sentences.text: It cleans the mouth, it protects the teeth and it's vital for digestion." Some studies also suggest that chewing can help with cognition.
sentences.article_title: Some dentists say more young people are grinding their teeth - are you one of them?

sentences.text: "We know this in animals, and our preliminary research is showing it in humans," he says.
sentences.article_title: Some dentists say more young people are grinding their teeth - are you one of them?

sentences.text: "By working our jaw muscles we are stimulating blood flow to the brain." But teeth grinding can also cause chronic pain, which can have a huge impact on your daily life.
sentences.article_title: Some dentists say more young people are grinding their teeth - are you one of them?

sentences.text: Dentist Riaz Yar, a specialist in prosthodontics, treats patients struggling with the effects of severe bruxism - worn, cracked and fractured teeth, and dental work that keeps failing.
sentences.article_title: Some dentists say more young people are grinding their teeth - are you one of them?

sentences.text: Many also arrive with chronic jaw or facial pain and report poor sleep, all of which need assessing in their own right, he says, rather than simply being blamed on the grinding.
sentences.article_title: Some dentists say more young people are grinding their teeth - are you one of them?

sentences.text: In the past, Yar says, teeth grinding was considered simply a mechanical problem of the jaw, but now there is strong evidence that it is much more complex.
sentences.article_title: Some dentists say more young people are grinding their teeth - are you one of them?

sentences.text: It's a "biopsychosocial issue", he says, driven by the brain and nervous system and shaped by the whole person.
sentences.article_title: Some dentists say more young people are grinding their teeth - are you one of them?

sentences.text: "We take into account their sleep patterns, their diet, their weight, the amount they exercise, what medication they might be taking and we assess for signs of sleep disorders," he says.
sentences.article_title: Some dentists say more young people are grinding their teeth - are you one of them?

sentences.text: "Many factors can contribute to a patient grinding their teeth, so addressing the condition requires a multidisciplinary approach." How best to tackle it?
sentences.article_title: Some dentists say more young people are grinding their teeth - are you one of them?

sentences.text: Hugo was strangled to death while staying in an NHS mental health unit Staff falsified records, slept and were on their phones on the night one patient was killed by another on an NHS mental health unit in east London, an inquest has heard.
sentences.article_title: Staff slept while patient killed at NHS mental health unit

sentences.text: Hugo Flint Cahan, 34, was being treated at Newham Mental Health Centre (NMHC), run by the East London NHS Trust (ELFT), when he was fatally attacked by 22-year-old Rolando Torres-Pena.

sentences.text: Have you ever slept next to a snoring partner and woken up feeling stressed, unfocused or forgetful the next day?
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: As snoring is relatively common, it is often left untreated and dismissed as a harmless irritation.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: But according to experts, sleeping next to a snorer could be impacting your health.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: Snoring is caused by the vibration of the soft tissues in our upper airways during sleep, explains Dr Clare Simon, a dentist with a special interest in dental sleep medicine.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: About 40% of the UK adult population snores, with the issue affecting more men than women, says the British Snoring and Sleep Apnoea Association (BSSAA).
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: And 75% of people with a snoring partner say they have had their sleep impacted, according to a US survey by the Sleep Foundation.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: Here's what you need to know about the impact on partners - and what you can do about it.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: Prof Ama Johal, a consultant orthodontist and sleep expert at Aerox Health, explains that the partner of a snorer can become "so impacted upon that it's almost a last-ditch effort on their part to get up and go sleep in a separate room because they have to sleep".
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: He adds: "As humans we physically can't function without that necessity." Prof Ama Johal says many couples put up with the negative effects snoring for too long During the night, we cycle through different stages of sleep in repeating patterns, usually every 90 minutes.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: The deeper stages of this cycle are important for physical restoration.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: If sleep is frequently disrupted, you may spend less time in the restorative stages, meaning you can wake up feeling tired, even if you've spent a lot of time in bed, the BSSAA explains.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: Your brain processes and stores information from the day during sleep.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: Fragmented sleep - which can happen if you're waking up due to a snoring partner - can interrupt this process, impacting your focus and memory.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: Disrupted sleep can also impact hormone regulation, which affects your energy levels and motivation.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: Sleep also plays a role in regulating the brain systems involved in stress and emotional response.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: When it is disrupted, these systems can become less balanced, which may make you feel more irritable and less able to cope with stress.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: This is something Meg Warren, 29, experienced when her former partner's snoring would keep her up.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: She says: "Without fail, after a snoring-induced wake up I would feel on incredibly high alert." Meg, a charity media officer, would prod him throughout the night and try to coax him from his back to his side.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: She says she would wake up "feeling groggy and dazed, sometimes so much so that it would feel like a hangover".
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: Meg Warren felt 'groggy and dazed' after a night of little sleep due to her former partner's snoring Anna-Louise Dearden, a 52-year-old journalist, says she sometimes sleeps in a separate room from her partner due to his snoring.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: Having this option allows her to prioritise getting enough rest when the snoring is particularly bad.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: There are things that can be done, say both Simon and Johal.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: But first, it is important to distinguish whether your partner is simply snoring, or whether they have sleep apnoea.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: "What you don't want to do is simply make someone quieter at night while potentially missing an underlying sleep-related breathing disorder," Simon says.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: Signs of sleep apnoea, a disorder that causes a person's breathing to repeatedly stop and start during sleep, include pauses in breathing, choking at night, waking frequently, and suffering from morning headaches.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: If this is what you are dealing with, you could be recommended a Continuous Positive Airway Pressure (CPAP) machine, or even surgical treatment in some cases, Simon explains.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: For simple snoring, Simon said that lifestyle changes can make a difference, such as losing weight, stopping smoking, reducing alcohol intake before bed, or changing your sleeping position - such as laying on your side rather than your back.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: You can also suggest to your partner that they see a GP, who will be able to advise further or refer you to a specialist.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: An expert might suggest treating nasal obstruction or allergies, if this is what is causing snoring, or wearing a custom mouthguard to gently push the lower jaw forward and keep the airway open.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: Johal says too many couples put up with snoring "for too long", which impacts their relationships and wellbeing.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health
