sentences.text: Friends Amelia (left) and Beatrice (right) are living at home when they start university this September More new students are choosing to live at home for university this year than in the last nine years, new data shows.
sentences.article_title: More students planning to live at home for university over 'insane' living costs

sentences.text: Over 81,000 UK 18-year-olds said in their accepted university application that they intended to live at home this year, according to the Universities and Colleges Admissions Service (Ucas) - just over one in three students in that category.
sentences.article_title: More students planning to live at home for university over 'insane' living costs

sentences.text: In 2017, it was closer to one in five.
sentences.article_title: More students planning to live at home for university over 'insane' living costs

sentences.text: The figures vary across the UK - with 48% of applicants in Scotland intending to live at home, compared with 20% in Wales - but the trend is rising across the board.
sentences.article_title: More students planning to live at home for university over 'insane' living costs

sentences.text: Students told the BBC the rising cost of living was a major influence in deciding what to do after school or college.
sentences.article_title: More students planning to live at home for university over 'insane' living costs

sentences.text: For friends Beatrice and Amelia, who are from St Helens, Merseyside, the cost of accommodation was a big factor in their decision to live at home while studying.
sentences.article_title: More students planning to live at home for university over 'insane' living costs

sentences.text: Both are heading to university in September, but neither will be moving into student accommodation.
sentences.article_title: More students planning to live at home for university over 'insane' living costs

sentences.text: Beatrice is going to the University of Manchester to study maths and plans to commute by train, a journey which can take about 50 minutes in total.
sentences.article_title: More students planning to live at home for university over 'insane' living costs

sentences.text: "My first choice was Manchester and then my second was Liverpool, so I knew I could commute," she says, adding that the price of accommodation would have been "a few grand a year".
sentences.article_title: More students planning to live at home for university over 'insane' living costs

sentences.text: Amelia, who is going to study at Liverpool John Moores University - approximately 20 minutes away by train - says the accommodation she found was between £300 and £400 a week.
sentences.article_title: More students planning to live at home for university over 'insane' living costs

sentences.text: Although neither is looking forward to the commute, both are still hoping they can get the full experience of university while living at home.
sentences.article_title: More students planning to live at home for university over 'insane' living costs

sentences.text: My three-hour university commute is worth the £7,000 saving on halls However, fellow student Jessica, who is also going to study at Liverpool John Moores University, feels she will miss out.
sentences.article_title: More students planning to live at home for university over 'insane' living costs

sentences.text: She says she would have loved to live on campus and enjoy student life, but the price of renting is "ridiculous" and "insane".
sentences.article_title: More students planning to live at home for university over 'insane' living costs

sentences.text: "I have a part-time job as everything is so expensive, and then commuting is going to kill a lot of my free time as well," she says.
sentences.article_title: More students planning to live at home for university over 'insane' living costs

sentences.text: "It is a bit sad really when you think about it." But she is pleased that staying at home means she will still be able to have her mum and dad's cooked dinners.
sentences.article_title: More students planning to live at home for university over 'insane' living costs

sentences.text: Earlier this year, BBC News followed the daily journey of one first-year student who said she was saving over £7,000 on accommodation by commuting 90 minutes into Manchester each day from home.
sentences.article_title: More students planning to live at home for university over 'insane' living costs

sentences.text: The figures were recorded on results day and are expected to rise over the coming month as more students accept university places through clearing.
sentences.article_title: More students planning to live at home for university over 'insane' living costs

sentences.text: A record number of UK 18-year-olds have been accepted into university this year.
sentences.article_title: More students planning to live at home for university over 'insane' living costs

sentences.text: But student rents have risen sharply in recent years, alongside other living costs.
sentences.article_title: More students planning to live at home for university over 'insane' living costs

sentences.text: The Higher Education Policy Institute (Hepi) said last year that students needed £61,000 over the course of a three-year degree in order to have a "minimum socially acceptable standard of living" - and that's excluding tuition fees.
sentences.article_title: More students planning to live at home for university over 'insane' living costs

sentences.text: Its report found that in 2024 the cost of renting in university-owned accommodation ranged from £108 per week, for 40 to 44-week contracts in Northern Ireland, to £338 a week for the shortest contracts in London, where rent makes up nearly half (46%) of students' costs.
sentences.article_title: More students planning to live at home for university over 'insane' living costs

sentences.text: In most areas it was between £140 and £180 a week, with private halls usually being more expensive.
sentences.article_title: More students planning to live at home for university over 'insane' living costs

sentences.text: Many students are eligible for a maintenance loan, which can help with the cost of accommodation, but the average annual price of a room on campus is increasing much faster, according to some student unions .
sentences.article_title: More students planning to live at home for university over 'insane' living costs

sentences.text: Hepi says most young full-time students now work in paid employment during term time to make up the difference between their maintenance loan income and the cost of living.
sentences.article_title: More students planning to live at home for university over 'insane' living costs

sentences.text: For some students, it means a rethink about what university looks like.
sentences.article_title: More students planning to live at home for university over 'insane' living costs

sentences.text: The Open University, which offers distance learning and online courses, says more teenagers than ever are starting courses with it.
sentences.article_title: More students planning to live at home for university over 'insane' living costs

sentences.text: Almost 3,400 18-and 19-year-olds joined the university last year – making up 9.5% of new starters, compared with 5.7% six years ago.
sentences.article_title: More students planning to live at home for university over 'insane' living costs

sentences.text: Traditionally, it has been popular with mature students wanting to continue working while studying from home.
sentences.article_title: More students planning to live at home for university over 'insane' living costs

sentences.text: Its vice-chancellor, Prof Dave Phoenix, says it points to a shift in how younger people are thinking about university, adding that studying online "means they can avoid moving costs and high accommodation bills and, for others, it means keeping a job".
sentences.article_title: More students planning to live at home for university over 'insane' living costs

sentences.text: But a recent report , external by Prof William Whyte, from the University of Oxford, argues that the value of on-campus life extends far beyond the price of accommodation, and plays an important role in personal development and the wider university experience.
sentences.article_title: More students planning to live at home for university over 'insane' living costs

sentences.text: "The question isn't simply where students live.
sentences.article_title: More students planning to live at home for university over 'insane' living costs

sentences.text: It's what they gain from living and learning together as part of a university community," he says.
sentences.article_title: More students planning to live at home for university over 'insane' living costs

sentences.text: "Currently, we have no real policy on accommodation for the overwhelming majority of students who want to leave home for study.
sentences.article_title: More students planning to live at home for university over 'insane' living costs

sentences.text: It's time for a serious debate about the role accommodation plays in the university – and how we will pay for it." A spokesperson for the Department for Education says the government recognises that too many students are facing financial hardship.
sentences.article_title: More students planning to live at home for university over 'insane' living costs

sentences.text: They say they are increasing maximum maintenance loans and reintroducing maintenance grants to help with living costs, as well as working with universities and councils to improve access to student housing.

sentences.text: Competition for degree apprenticeships in England has quadrupled over the past three years, the BBC has found.
sentences.article_title: Competition for degree apprenticeships quadruples as university costs rise

sentences.text: The popularity of degree apprenticeships - which offer a paid-for university degree along with a salary - has grown as the cost of university has come under increased scrutiny.
sentences.article_title: Competition for degree apprenticeships quadruples as university costs rise

sentences.text: Data seen by the BBC showed the number of applicants through the government's central platform nearly tripled from 8,100 to 21,800 over the past three years, while the number of positions available fell by almost half, from 7,300 to 3,700.
sentences.article_title: Competition for degree apprenticeships quadruples as university costs rise

sentences.text: Applicants said they applied to university as a "backup" because competition was so fierce, with employers cutting back on hiring because of high employment costs and economic uncertainty.
sentences.article_title: Competition for degree apprenticeships quadruples as university costs rise

sentences.text: African wild dogs are extraordinary long-distance travellers A pack of African wild dogs has completed a record-breaking 2,485-mile (4000km) journey across Zambia.
sentences.article_title: Wild dogs record 2,500-mile trek across Zambia in search of a mate

sentences.text: Scientists say it is the furthest recorded distance for any African land mammal searching for a mate, offering hope that wildlife can travel across vast distances despite growing human pressures.
sentences.article_title: Wild dogs record 2,500-mile trek across Zambia in search of a mate

sentences.text: The three brothers zigzagged across Zambia, navigating a landscape increasingly shaped by people and avoiding obstacles including major cities.
sentences.article_title: Wild dogs record 2,500-mile trek across Zambia in search of a mate

sentences.text: However, other wild dogs tracked with GPS collars in the study died in illegal snares, underlining the dangers they face.
sentences.article_title: Wild dogs record 2,500-mile trek across Zambia in search of a mate

sentences.text: Spreading human communities break up their once-vast roaming grounds Three sisters almost completed an equally epic journey, but stopped when one became trapped in a snare.
sentences.article_title: Wild dogs record 2,500-mile trek across Zambia in search of a mate

sentences.text: African wild dogs are among Africa's rarest predators, with only about 6,000 remaining in the wild.
sentences.article_title: Wild dogs record 2,500-mile trek across Zambia in search of a mate

sentences.text: They live in highly social packs, hunt together and are known for their vast roaming in search of new territory and breeding opportunities with other packs.
sentences.article_title: Wild dogs record 2,500-mile trek across Zambia in search of a mate

sentences.text: They cannot breed within the pack they are born into, so they either wait and may eventually inherit their pack, or set off at the age of two or three in search of a mate.
sentences.article_title: Wild dogs record 2,500-mile trek across Zambia in search of a mate

sentences.text: The brothers covered about 260 miles in a straight line over the course of eight months, but travelled nearly 10 times that overall while crossing through a broken-up landscape.
sentences.article_title: Wild dogs record 2,500-mile trek across Zambia in search of a mate

sentences.text: These sorts of journeys are known as dispersals - travelling one way in search of a mate, which is a behaviour distinct from migrations, where animals move back and forth with the seasons in search of food or habitat.
sentences.article_title: Wild dogs record 2,500-mile trek across Zambia in search of a mate

sentences.text: The UN Convention on Migratory Species identifies Africa's longest migrations as wildebeest moving seasonally between Tanzania and Kenya in search of grazing and water covering more than 400 miles.
sentences.article_title: Wild dogs record 2,500-mile trek across Zambia in search of a mate

sentences.text: Globally, caribou undertake the longest single land migrations of any animal - travelling 839 miles in a round trip, while grey wolves have been recorded travelling more than 4,350 miles over a year.
sentences.article_title: Wild dogs record 2,500-mile trek across Zambia in search of a mate

sentences.text: Perhaps even more significant than the distance itself was the route the wild dogs took through Zambia.
sentences.article_title: Wild dogs record 2,500-mile trek across Zambia in search of a mate

sentences.text: They moved between wildlife strongholds, skirting areas containing major human obstacles, including the capital, Lusaka, and heavily developed industrial areas.
sentences.article_title: Wild dogs record 2,500-mile trek across Zambia in search of a mate

sentences.text: The findings suggest wild dog populations across eastern and southern Africa may remain more connected than conservationists previously believed.
sentences.article_title: Wild dogs record 2,500-mile trek across Zambia in search of a mate

sentences.text: Professor Scott Creel of Montana State University, the paper's lead author, who has been studying African wild dogs since 1991, said the study provides cautious optimism.
sentences.article_title: Wild dogs record 2,500-mile trek across Zambia in search of a mate

sentences.text: "It's plausible to believe that every major wild dog population in eastern and southern Africa, other than fenced ones, are potentially connected," he said.
sentences.article_title: Wild dogs record 2,500-mile trek across Zambia in search of a mate

sentences.text: But he said, in conservation,"the glass is half empty and the glass is half full", highlighting the threat of poaching snares.
sentences.article_title: Wild dogs record 2,500-mile trek across Zambia in search of a mate

sentences.text: While the three male wild dogs successfully completed their extraordinary journey, two of the three females died.
sentences.article_title: Wild dogs record 2,500-mile trek across Zambia in search of a mate

sentences.text: Researchers identified a pattern in which surviving pack members repeatedly returned to the same location, a behaviour that often signals the death of a companion.
sentences.article_title: Wild dogs record 2,500-mile trek across Zambia in search of a mate

sentences.text: The research, published in the journal, Ecology , external , adds weight to calls to create strips of natural land outside protected areas that connect separate wildlife areas broken apart by roads, towns, or farms.
sentences.article_title: Wild dogs record 2,500-mile trek across Zambia in search of a mate

sentences.text: Bruce Ellender, one of the paper's co-authors and Kafue Conservation director for the environmental charity, The Nature Conservancy, said species that roam over large areas, such as wild dogs and elephants, need connected landscapes if they are to survive into the future.
sentences.article_title: Wild dogs record 2,500-mile trek across Zambia in search of a mate

sentences.text: "We can't see these protected areas as islands and expect them to be functional in the long term, we need to think much broader than that," he said.

sentences.article_title: Rare tree offspring given lifeline at Scottish botanic garden

sentences.text: The marina said there were limited options available for disposal sites A wildlife trust has called for a new offshore disposal site to be found for sediment dredged from Brighton Marina, saying it remains concerned about plans being explored off Newhaven.
sentences.article_title: Wildlife trust wants marina silt disposed offshore

sentences.text: Brighton Marina has been looking for a long-term disposal site since Sussex Wildlife Trust successfully challenged a licence in 2025 for disposal of sediment at Rottingdean.
sentences.article_title: Wildlife trust wants marina silt disposed offshore

sentences.text: The marina has said dredging is needed to maintain safe access and there are limited options available for disposal sites.
sentences.article_title: Wildlife trust wants marina silt disposed offshore

sentences.text: Sussex Wildlife Trust said Newhaven was a "protected area" that sat adjacent to the Beachy Head West Marine Conservation Zone (MCZ).
sentences.article_title: Wildlife trust wants marina silt disposed offshore

sentences.text: Campaigners previously claimed the silt was a " black, thick, slimy, petrochemically smelling sludge ", but Premier Marinas, which owns Brighton Marina, said dredged silt was regularly sampled to confirm it was not harmful.
sentences.article_title: Wildlife trust wants marina silt disposed offshore

sentences.text: Protesters opposed the use of Rottingdean in a demo by the marina in January 2025 John Cervenka, Premier Marinas chief operating officer, said: "Maintaining safe navigational access to Brighton Marina is not optional.
sentences.article_title: Wildlife trust wants marina silt disposed offshore

sentences.text: It is a legal requirement and fundamental to the operation of the marina." He said the marina was a major centre of economic activity.
sentences.article_title: Wildlife trust wants marina silt disposed offshore

sentences.text: According to the marina, about 150 businesses depend on the site, creating jobs for about 1,200 people, with more than eight million visits each year.
sentences.article_title: Wildlife trust wants marina silt disposed offshore

sentences.text: Premier Marinas said Newhaven had been identified as a potential alternative by Sussex Wildlife Trust.
sentences.article_title: Wildlife trust wants marina silt disposed offshore

sentences.text: "Our preferred option is a new offshore disposal site, well away from the MCZ." The trust said that Newhaven was already used for dredge disposal by Newhaven Port, and there was currently no available data on the impacts of additional disposal there.
sentences.article_title: Wildlife trust wants marina silt disposed offshore

sentences.text: Until it saw further evidence, it did not have a view on whether Newhaven was suitable, it added.
sentences.article_title: Wildlife trust wants marina silt disposed offshore

sentences.text: "We will respond to any future licence application based on the ecological evidence it contains," it said.
sentences.article_title: Wildlife trust wants marina silt disposed offshore

sentences.text: Brighton Marina hopes to submit a marine licence application to the Marine Management Organisation in November.
sentences.article_title: Wildlife trust wants marina silt disposed offshore

sentences.text: If approved, maintenance dredging could restart next spring.

sentences.text: India's government says 56 glacial lakes had been classified as "very high risk" The Himalayas are approaching a dangerous threshold as glaciers melt faster, glacial lakes grow more unstable and the mountains face a widening gap in monitoring, according to new research.
sentences.article_title: The Himalayas are melting faster - and India's economy is 'at risk'

sentences.text: The findings come in the aftermath of devastating floods in Nepal and Tibet, which killed more than 1,300 people and caused widespread destruction, highlighting the growing risks from a rapidly changing Himalayan environment.
sentences.article_title: The Himalayas are melting faster - and India's economy is 'at risk'

sentences.text: Yet only about 21 of the estimated 40,000 glaciers across the Himalaya-Karakoram region are being monitored in detail and on a sustained basis, according to the report.
sentences.article_title: The Himalayas are melting faster - and India's economy is 'at risk'

sentences.text: That monitoring gap matters because the physical landscape is changing rapidly.
sentences.article_title: The Himalayas are melting faster - and India's economy is 'at risk'

sentences.text: As glaciers retreat, they can leave behind expanding lakes held back by unstable deposits of rock and ice.
sentences.article_title: The Himalayas are melting faster - and India's economy is 'at risk'

sentences.text: At the same time, warming is destabilising permafrost - permanently frozen ground that can thaw as temperatures rise - and high mountain slopes, increasing the possibility of cascading hazards, the report says.
sentences.article_title: The Himalayas are melting faster - and India's economy is 'at risk'

sentences.text: A glacial lake outburst in 2023 triggered a flash flood, causing extensive damage in Sikkim India already has evidence of the scale of the risk.
sentences.article_title: The Himalayas are melting faster - and India's economy is 'at risk'

sentences.text: Some 18% of Indian land is Himalayan, yet the region accounts for about 35% of disasters, according to the report.
sentences.article_title: The Himalayas are melting faster - and India's economy is 'at risk'

sentences.text: The government told parliament in July that 56 glacial lakes had been classified as "very high risk" , external following a 2025 scientific assessment of 189 high-risk lakes in the Indian Himalayan region.
sentences.article_title: The Himalayas are melting faster - and India's economy is 'at risk'

sentences.text: The Central Water Commission is monitoring 2,485 glacial lakes larger than 10 hectares across India's Himalayan river basins, the government said.
sentences.article_title: The Himalayas are melting faster - and India's economy is 'at risk'

sentences.text: The Himalayas have already seen devastating examples of what can happen when glacial lakes burst their natural dams.
sentences.article_title: The Himalayas are melting faster - and India's economy is 'at risk'

sentences.text: In 2023, a glacial lake outburst flood in Sikkim killed at least 70 people and caused widespread damage to roads, bridges and hydropower projects.
sentences.article_title: The Himalayas are melting faster - and India's economy is 'at risk'

sentences.text: In 2021, a similar disaster in Uttarakhand killed more than 200 people after a massive flood swept through the Rishiganga and Dhauliganga valleys.
sentences.article_title: The Himalayas are melting faster - and India's economy is 'at risk'

sentences.text: But the danger is not confined to spectacular floods.
sentences.article_title: The Himalayas are melting faster - and India's economy is 'at risk'

sentences.text: The Himalayas are a vast natural water system feeding rivers that sustain hundreds of millions of people across South Asia.
sentences.article_title: The Himalayas are melting faster - and India's economy is 'at risk'

sentences.text: ICIMOD says "peak water" , external is expected around mid-century in most Hindu Kush Himalayan river basins - the point at which glacier runoff reaches its maximum before declining as glaciers lose mass.
sentences.article_title: The Himalayas are melting faster - and India's economy is 'at risk'

sentences.text: The new research puts an unusually large economic number on that dependency.
sentences.article_title: The Himalayas are melting faster - and India's economy is 'at risk'

sentences.text: It estimates that Himalayan water underpins roughly 20% of India's GDP, sustaining wheat, rice, tea, hydropower and pilgrimage economies.
sentences.article_title: The Himalayas are melting faster - and India's economy is 'at risk'

sentences.text: Yet the mountain states capture only about 5% of that value, it says.
sentences.article_title: The Himalayas are melting faster - and India's economy is 'at risk'

sentences.text: "The Himalayas are the Third Pole," said economist Lord Nicholas Stern, chair of the Grantham Research Institute on Climate Change and the Environment at the London School of Economics.
sentences.article_title: The Himalayas are melting faster - and India's economy is 'at risk'

sentences.text: "Unlike the Arctic or Antarctic, this pole has hundreds of millions of people living beneath it." The Indian Himalayan region receives roughly 400 million visits a year "This is national and international infrastructure," he said, warning that the ecological system underpinning it is "approaching a tipping point".
sentences.article_title: The Himalayas are melting faster - and India's economy is 'at risk'

sentences.text: Not all the forces driving glacier loss are beyond the region's control.
sentences.article_title: The Himalayas are melting faster - and India's economy is 'at risk'

sentences.text: The Systemiq research estimates that roughly a third of Himalayan glacier melt is driven by black carbon, much of it originating from brick kilns in the plains.
sentences.article_title: The Himalayas are melting faster - and India's economy is 'at risk'

sentences.text: Soot deposited on snow and ice absorbs more sunlight and accelerates melting.
sentences.article_title: The Himalayas are melting faster - and India's economy is 'at risk'

sentences.text: Unlike global greenhouse-gas emissions, black-carbon pollution is a lever that India and its neighbours can act on directly, the report argues.
sentences.article_title: The Himalayas are melting faster - and India's economy is 'at risk'

sentences.text: "The Himalayas are approaching a tipping point, with millions of lives and livelihoods hanging in the balance," said Arushi Chopra, Systemiq's senior director and lead author.
sentences.article_title: The Himalayas are melting faster - and India's economy is 'at risk'

sentences.text: "Glaciers are melting faster than they were a decade ago." The report proposes 10 priority transitions, ranging from reducing black-carbon emissions and expanding glacier monitoring to improving disaster early-warning systems and changing the way tourism is developed in the mountains.
sentences.article_title: The Himalayas are melting faster - and India's economy is 'at risk'

sentences.text: One priority is to strengthen disaster preparedness, with governments agreeing in advance what action to take when hazards emerge - from evacuation to protecting vulnerable infrastructure.
sentences.article_title: The Himalayas are melting faster - and India's economy is 'at risk'

sentences.text: Another is to rethink tourism.
sentences.article_title: The Himalayas are melting faster - and India's economy is 'at risk'

sentences.text: The Indian Himalayan region receives roughly 400 million tourist visits a year, according to the report, and researchers argue that the objective should shift from maximising visitor numbers towards generating value that is retained and reinvested locally.
sentences.article_title: The Himalayas are melting faster - and India's economy is 'at risk'

sentences.text: Pema Gyamtsho, director general of ICIMOD, said the risks were becoming increasingly complex.
sentences.article_title: The Himalayas are melting faster - and India's economy is 'at risk'

sentences.text: "Glaciers are retreating, permafrost and high-mountain slopes are becoming increasingly unstable, and communities and infrastructure downstream face growing risks from complex and cascading hazards," he said.
sentences.article_title: The Himalayas are melting faster - and India's economy is 'at risk'

sentences.text: And those risks do not stop at the borders drawn across the Himalayas.
sentences.article_title: The Himalayas are melting faster - and India's economy is 'at risk'

sentences.text: Such hazards, Gyamtsho said, "do not respect national borders, and no single country can address them alone".
sentences.article_title: The Himalayas are melting faster - and India's economy is 'at risk'

sentences.text: That makes cross-border monitoring, shared risk information and early-warning systems, and joint investment in resilience increasingly urgent - not just to save lives, but to protect the livelihoods and economies of hundreds of millions of people who depend on the mountains.
sentences.article_title: The Himalayas are melting faster - and India's economy is 'at risk'

sentences.text: Professor Dave Chadwick from Bangor University sampling damaged remains following wildfires at Mynydd Llangynidr in Bannau Brycheiniog Scientists investigating the damage caused by severe wildfires across Wales this summer say the impact has been "catastrophic".
sentences.article_title: Summer wildfires caused catastrophic hidden damage, scientists warn

sentences.text: Extreme heat and exceptionally dry conditions throughout July and August left landscapes such as heathland, moorland and upland grasslands vulnerable to fast spreading fires, resulting in one of the UK's worst wildfire seasons in recent years.
sentences.article_title: Summer wildfires caused catastrophic hidden damage, scientists warn

sentences.text: Prof Davey Jones, who is leading a Bangor University survey of several sites across Wales, said the scale of damage was far greater than what was immediately visible.
sentences.article_title: Summer wildfires caused catastrophic hidden damage, scientists warn

sentences.text: "People see the blackened vegetation and assume that's the main impact, but the real story is below our feet," said Jones.
sentences.article_title: Summer wildfires caused catastrophic hidden damage, scientists warn

sentences.text: During the July peak, fires affected approximately 2,760 acres of countryside across north Wales alone, the equivalent of more than 1,500 football pitches.
sentences.article_title: Summer wildfires caused catastrophic hidden damage, scientists warn

sentences.text: At Sychnant Pass in Conwy county, one of the most significant blazes saw 36 homes having to be evacuated and about 200 acres of land affected.
sentences.article_title: Summer wildfires caused catastrophic hidden damage, scientists warn

sentences.text: Prof Davey Jones said the scale of damage from the wildfires was far greater than what was immediately visible At Sychnant Pass today, there are slight green shoots of recovery visible among the charred hillside.
sentences.article_title: Summer wildfires caused catastrophic hidden damage, scientists warn

sentences.text: But Jones described a rare ecosystem housing specialist plants, butterflies and insects, "where the UK is the epicentre globally".
sentences.article_title: Summer wildfires caused catastrophic hidden damage, scientists warn

sentences.text: "We've probably lost about 10 centimetres of soil here [at Sychnant Pass] so we've lost all of that organic matter layer... 4,000 years of carbon gone in a single event," he said.
sentences.article_title: Summer wildfires caused catastrophic hidden damage, scientists warn

sentences.text: "Once the topsoil is gone, we can never recover that.
sentences.article_title: Summer wildfires caused catastrophic hidden damage, scientists warn

sentences.text: "People see the blackened vegetation and assume that's the main impact, but the real story is below our feet.
sentences.article_title: Summer wildfires caused catastrophic hidden damage, scientists warn

sentences.text: "This soil acts as a water sponge, a carbon store, a nutrient bank.
sentences.article_title: Summer wildfires caused catastrophic hidden damage, scientists warn

sentences.text: "Losing it is a double whammy, it worsens climate change and makes the habitat far more fragile." He added: "This site has taken thousands of years to develop and it's all gone in maybe five days?
sentences.article_title: Summer wildfires caused catastrophic hidden damage, scientists warn

sentences.text: "If we are going to try and put that soil back, generate artificial soils through the reuse of organic wastes for example, then it's important we understand what the soil quality is now.
sentences.article_title: Summer wildfires caused catastrophic hidden damage, scientists warn

sentences.text: "So that we can prepare for the future and design those soils, because they don't exist yet." Over recent weeks the Bangor team has been racing to collect soil samples at several sites across Wales before heavy winter rainfall washes away the remains.
sentences.article_title: Summer wildfires caused catastrophic hidden damage, scientists warn

sentences.text: Their work has included comparing the burnt land with adjacent untouched areas, allowing researchers to measure changes in soil carbon, nutrients, microbial activity, water repellency and erosion risk.
sentences.article_title: Summer wildfires caused catastrophic hidden damage, scientists warn

sentences.text: Even NASA satellite data has been used to quickly identify new sites after fires have occurred.
sentences.article_title: Summer wildfires caused catastrophic hidden damage, scientists warn

sentences.text: Dr Kara Marsden says responding quickly is key Dr Kara Marsden, a lecturer in soil science who is also working on the project, said working at speed was vital.
sentences.article_title: Summer wildfires caused catastrophic hidden damage, scientists warn

sentences.text: "It was really important that we got on site very quickly to measure the soil and vegetation properties while the fire's impacts were still fresh," she said.
sentences.article_title: Summer wildfires caused catastrophic hidden damage, scientists warn

sentences.text: "These things can change rapidly, so capturing that baseline data now means we'll have something accurate to compare against in future sampling dates." She warned that early green shoots now visible at the site did not necessarily reflect true or full recovery.
sentences.article_title: Summer wildfires caused catastrophic hidden damage, scientists warn

sentences.text: "Bracken sprouts almost immediately because its rhizomes sit deep in the soil, so the burn layer wouldn't maybe have impacted those" she said.
sentences.article_title: Summer wildfires caused catastrophic hidden damage, scientists warn

sentences.text: "But the heather and gorse have much shallower roots, so you know they're completely gone.
sentences.article_title: Summer wildfires caused catastrophic hidden damage, scientists warn

sentences.text: "They've been completely lost... that depth of soil they depend on could take thousands of years to form again." Jones said that the impact of such wildfires extended far beyond biodiversity loss.
sentences.article_title: Summer wildfires caused catastrophic hidden damage, scientists warn

sentences.text: "Fires release carbon, nitrogen and sulphur back into the atmosphere, in itself contributing to climate change," he said.
sentences.article_title: Summer wildfires caused catastrophic hidden damage, scientists warn

sentences.text: "Every time we have a wildfire, we're just making the problem worse and worse.
sentences.article_title: Summer wildfires caused catastrophic hidden damage, scientists warn

sentences.text: "It becomes a self‑sustaining cycle... drier soils, more fires, more carbon released." He also warned that without rapid restoration and better wildfire preparedness, "we might lose pretty much all of this habitat within our lifetime".
sentences.article_title: Summer wildfires caused catastrophic hidden damage, scientists warn

sentences.text: Researchers will return to the sites over the next two years to track recovery and assess whether some habitats are more resilient than others.
sentences.article_title: Summer wildfires caused catastrophic hidden damage, scientists warn

sentences.text: Early evidence suggests vegetation can return, but more slowly and more fragile, leaving landscapes increasingly susceptible to future burns.
sentences.article_title: Summer wildfires caused catastrophic hidden damage, scientists warn

sentences.text: Champagne lovers may find themselves getting tipsy more quickly after French producers have been given the go-ahead to raise the alcohol content in a bottle of bubbly for the first time following this summer's record heatwave.
sentences.article_title: Record heatwaves in France set to make champagne stronger

sentences.text: Winemakers can temporarily produce champagne with an alcohol content of up to 15% -  above the 13% cap, industry officials have said.
sentences.article_title: Record heatwaves in France set to make champagne stronger

sentences.text: The extreme heat and drought produced grapes with exceptionally higher sugar levels.
sentences.article_title: Record heatwaves in France set to make champagne stronger

sentences.text: Yeast converts sugar into alcohol during fermentation.
sentences.article_title: Record heatwaves in France set to make champagne stronger

sentences.text: France's Champagne region also saw its earliest-ever harvest due to the weather, something that could become the norm "in 10 to 15 years" because of climate change, according to the Comite Champagne industry association.
sentences.article_title: Record heatwaves in France set to make champagne stronger

sentences.text: How will extreme weather affect our food?
sentences.article_title: Record heatwaves in France set to make champagne stronger

sentences.text: France links sharp rise in drownings to heatwaves The temporary increase in champagne's alcohol content is only expected to affect a small number of wines, a spokeswoman for the Comite Champagne told the BBC.
sentences.article_title: Record heatwaves in France set to make champagne stronger

sentences.text: During the second fermentation process, which gives champagne its bubbles, "a very small number of wines from this harvest could have slightly exceeded the regulatory limit of 13%, reaching around 13.1% or 13.2%".
sentences.article_title: Record heatwaves in France set to make champagne stronger

sentences.text: "Therefore a decision was made to exceptionally and temporarily increase the regulatory limit to 15%  - only for this year," she said.
sentences.article_title: Record heatwaves in France set to make champagne stronger

sentences.text: The first grapes were cut in early August and the harvest expanded by the middle of the month, "the earliest ever recorded in Champagne", the association said.
sentences.article_title: Record heatwaves in France set to make champagne stronger

sentences.text: "The 2026 growing season will be remembered as one of the most unusual in Champagne's history, marked by severe spring frosts of historic intensity, an exceptionally early flowering period and five heatwaves throughout the summer." it added.
sentences.article_title: Record heatwaves in France set to make champagne stronger

sentences.text: Speaking in the Times newspaper, Stéphane Vignon, a producer in Verzenay said: "The Mediterranean climate is moving north.
sentences.article_title: Record heatwaves in France set to make champagne stronger

sentences.text: This is year one of a new cycle.
sentences.article_title: Record heatwaves in France set to make champagne stronger

sentences.text: It's unlikely to be every year, but it will happen again".
sentences.article_title: Record heatwaves in France set to make champagne stronger

sentences.text: Higher-strength champagne is unlikely to be an obvious selling point, warned Jane Anson, a wine columnist and author based in Bordeaux.
sentences.article_title: Record heatwaves in France set to make champagne stronger

sentences.text: She told the Times: "Today people increasingly prefer lower-alcohol "The battle between what consumers want and what nature provides must be very stressful for producers." The 2026 vintage is unlikely to hit shelves until 2028 as champagne must age for at least 15 months.
sentences.article_title: Record heatwaves in France set to make champagne stronger

sentences.text: Grape harvesting began early in France this year Maxime Toubart, co-chair of the Comite Champagne, told the AFP news agency that the likelihood of hotter weather in the future means "this unusual harvest will probably become the norm in 10 to 15 years".
sentences.article_title: Record heatwaves in France set to make champagne stronger

sentences.text: France has been one of Europe's worst-hit countries during this year's extreme weather, sparking huge wildfires .
sentences.article_title: Record heatwaves in France set to make champagne stronger

sentences.text: Climate change is driving up global average temperatures, making heatwaves more frequent and intense.
sentences.article_title: Record heatwaves in France set to make champagne stronger

sentences.text: Alcohol buyers will be able to use a digital ID app on their phones to prove their age under new rules introduced on Tuesday.
sentences.article_title: Pubs in England and Wales to allow digital ID apps to prove age

sentences.text: Pubs and shops in England and Wales can use the tech in addition to current physical forms of ID - with the government saying a digital option will make age-checks quicker and more secure for customers and staff.
sentences.article_title: Pubs in England and Wales to allow digital ID apps to prove age

sentences.text: Customers will be able to choose ID apps from a range of suppliers such as the Post Office, Yoti or Luciditi, provided they are on a government-approved list.
sentences.article_title: Pubs in England and Wales to allow digital ID apps to prove age

sentences.text: The change means businesses will no longer be required to let people use physical ID, but the government contends most establishments would.
sentences.article_title: Pubs in England and Wales to allow digital ID apps to prove age

sentences.text: The plan will be technology-agnostic, meaning that the government is not setting out in detail how each app must work.
sentences.article_title: Pubs in England and Wales to allow digital ID apps to prove age

sentences.text: It argues that under the voluntary digital ID scheme, drinkers would share fewer personal details with a venue or shop - such as tapping their phone on a reader or displaying a scannable QR code rather than handing over an official document.
sentences.article_title: Pubs in England and Wales to allow digital ID apps to prove age

sentences.text: The apps will also need to guard against customers borrowing devices from older friends and relatives, and ensure the ID app belongs to the person using it.
sentences.article_title: Pubs in England and Wales to allow digital ID apps to prove age

sentences.text: Yoti's digital ID app, for example, will only let a user log in if a scan of their face matches that of the person who signed up for the app.
sentences.article_title: Pubs in England and Wales to allow digital ID apps to prove age

sentences.text: The app then generates a QR code that can be scanned by a business with a free checker app, which tells them the person's age.
sentences.article_title: Pubs in England and Wales to allow digital ID apps to prove age

sentences.text: This is time-limited to make duping or sharing the QR code more difficult.
sentences.article_title: Pubs in England and Wales to allow digital ID apps to prove age

sentences.text: Digital government minister Stephanie Peacock said having the option for digital ID would "mean you do not need to carry a physical ID, nor hand over sensitive personal information" meaning people could "feel safer on a night out'".
sentences.article_title: Pubs in England and Wales to allow digital ID apps to prove age

sentences.text: Allen Simpson, chief executive of trade body UKHospitality, said the new rules were a "positive step".
sentences.article_title: Pubs in England and Wales to allow digital ID apps to prove age

sentences.text: He added the industry would work with government to make sure the scheme's roll-out would not be "burdensome" for the hospitality sector.
sentences.article_title: Pubs in England and Wales to allow digital ID apps to prove age

sentences.text: This would include ensuring there were multiple options for suppliers and that it was cost-efficient, Simpson said.
sentences.article_title: Pubs in England and Wales to allow digital ID apps to prove age

sentences.text: The government wants digital ID apps under its scheme to work together so customers do not need to use different apps in different venues.
sentences.article_title: Pubs in England and Wales to allow digital ID apps to prove age

sentences.text: It also wants the services to work offline and accessible even without mobile data or a Wi-Fi connection.
sentences.article_title: Pubs in England and Wales to allow digital ID apps to prove age

sentences.text: In future, the digital proof of age scheme could be extended to cover tobacco and vapes.
sentences.article_title: Pubs in England and Wales to allow digital ID apps to prove age

sentences.text: But digital rights campaigners have said such measures could lead to the exclusion of some groups.
sentences.article_title: Pubs in England and Wales to allow digital ID apps to prove age

sentences.text: Jasleen Chaggar of Big Brother Watch said while having multiple ways to prove your identity was helpful, the Government should ensure that digital ID did not become effectively mandatory "as it would shut out millions of people".
sentences.article_title: Pubs in England and Wales to allow digital ID apps to prove age

sentences.text: "Many people have legitimate reasons for relying on physical ID, whether out of choice, privacy and security concerns, or because they lack the digital skills or means to use digital ID," she said.
sentences.article_title: Pubs in England and Wales to allow digital ID apps to prove age

sentences.text: "The Government should expressly prohibit businesses from requiring digital IDs for age checks without offering reasonable alternatives," she added.
sentences.article_title: Pubs in England and Wales to allow digital ID apps to prove age

sentences.text: The new rules come after a wider digital ID programme promoted by former Prime Minister Sir Keir Starmer proved controversial , and was later abandoned by Andy Burnham.
sentences.article_title: Pubs in England and Wales to allow digital ID apps to prove age

sentences.text: This video can not be played Watch: BBC’s Tom Gerken gets his hands on Valve's Steam Frame Valve's new virtual reality headset, the Steam Frame, has officially been released - but it comes at a high price.
sentences.article_title: Valve's Steam Frame is excellent - but at over £1,000 is VR still too expensive?

sentences.text: The hardware is excellent - a light device which feels comfortable to wear and is packed with clever technology - so long as you're willing to pay a whopping £1,089 for a headset with 1TB of storage.
sentences.article_title: Valve's Steam Frame is excellent - but at over £1,000 is VR still too expensive?

sentences.text: The variant with 256GB of storage, meanwhile, costs £889.
sentences.article_title: Valve's Steam Frame is excellent - but at over £1,000 is VR still too expensive?

sentences.text: Both are capable of streaming from a PC as well as playing games on-device, with varying degrees of success.
sentences.article_title: Valve's Steam Frame is excellent - but at over £1,000 is VR still too expensive?

sentences.text: But it carries a price tag which will make a lot of people roll their eyes, and doesn't do much to dispel criticism that increasingly-costly VR headsets are pricing people out of the hobby.
sentences.article_title: Valve's Steam Frame is excellent - but at over £1,000 is VR still too expensive?

sentences.text: But before we get into that hefty price tag, is the Steam Frame actually any good?
sentences.article_title: Valve's Steam Frame is excellent - but at over £1,000 is VR still too expensive?

sentences.text: I've owned VR headsets for well over a decade, and Valve's latest effort makes a promising first impression.
sentences.article_title: Valve's Steam Frame is excellent - but at over £1,000 is VR still too expensive?

sentences.text: Games run well - really the bare minimum considering the price tag - and it's easy enough to use.
sentences.article_title: Valve's Steam Frame is excellent - but at over £1,000 is VR still too expensive?

sentences.text: Puzzle games like the VR version of Escape Simulator - which tasks you with solving puzzles to exit a room - run great, as you would hope One of the nice things is, like Meta's Quest 3, it has flat "pancake" lenses allowing you to see clearly when you put the headset on.
sentences.article_title: Valve's Steam Frame is excellent - but at over £1,000 is VR still too expensive?

sentences.text: It's light - weighing little more than a can of soup.
sentences.article_title: Valve's Steam Frame is excellent - but at over £1,000 is VR still too expensive?

sentences.text: But what makes it comfortable is the decision to separate the internals up.
sentences.article_title: Valve's Steam Frame is excellent - but at over £1,000 is VR still too expensive?

sentences.text: The battery pack rests on the back of your head while the screen is at the front - meaning you don't feel front-heavy, a common criticism of other headsets.
sentences.article_title: Valve's Steam Frame is excellent - but at over £1,000 is VR still too expensive?

sentences.text: But there are better screens out there.
sentences.article_title: Valve's Steam Frame is excellent - but at over £1,000 is VR still too expensive?

sentences.text: The PlayStation VR2 for example has incredible OLED displays, albeit without the pancake lenses.
sentences.article_title: Valve's Steam Frame is excellent - but at over £1,000 is VR still too expensive?

sentences.text: Apple and Samsung both have excellent screens too in their own headsets.
sentences.article_title: Valve's Steam Frame is excellent - but at over £1,000 is VR still too expensive?

sentences.text: Yet these come at a serious premium, costing significantly more than the Steam Frame.
sentences.article_title: Valve's Steam Frame is excellent - but at over £1,000 is VR still too expensive?

sentences.text: Moss sees you guide a mouse through a series of environments which look excellent in a VR headset - even if a flat screenshot doesn't quite do it justice When Meta launched the Quest 3 in June 2023, its 128GB model retailed for £480.
sentences.article_title: Valve's Steam Frame is excellent - but at over £1,000 is VR still too expensive?

sentences.text: Less storage, but a much lower price.
sentences.article_title: Valve's Steam Frame is excellent - but at over £1,000 is VR still too expensive?

sentences.text: Three years later, it's hard to believe VR just keeps getting more expensive when the Quest 3 felt like a turning point.
sentences.article_title: Valve's Steam Frame is excellent - but at over £1,000 is VR still too expensive?

sentences.text: "VR today is ultimately a high-end niche," gaming writer Christopher Dring told me.
sentences.article_title: Valve's Steam Frame is excellent - but at over £1,000 is VR still too expensive?

sentences.text: "Meta had been subsidising the Quest hardware, and it's difficult to imagine they will going forward as they pivot away from those experiences." Of course, there are reasons for prices going up.
sentences.article_title: Valve's Steam Frame is excellent - but at over £1,000 is VR still too expensive?

sentences.text: AI developers are building giant data centres filled with racks of powerful servers, using many of the same components needed to make devices like the Steam Frame.
sentences.article_title: Valve's Steam Frame is excellent - but at over £1,000 is VR still too expensive?

sentences.text: Ram prices alone more than doubled in price between October 2025 and the start of 2026 .
sentences.article_title: Valve's Steam Frame is excellent - but at over £1,000 is VR still too expensive?

sentences.text: Meanwhile, the graphics card I bought for £500 a few months ago now sits at closer to £650.
sentences.article_title: Valve's Steam Frame is excellent - but at over £1,000 is VR still too expensive?

sentences.text: As prices climb higher and higher, hardware developers don't have much of a choice but to put up their own.
sentences.article_title: Valve's Steam Frame is excellent - but at over £1,000 is VR still too expensive?

sentences.text: "We set out to come out with a device that would have been much more affordable," Valve developer Jeremy Selan said.
sentences.article_title: Valve's Steam Frame is excellent - but at over £1,000 is VR still too expensive?

sentences.text: "But the global Ram market has impacted us the same way it's impacted everybody." Selan said the firm "fought hard to get it even to this price" and made the decision to ship the Steam Frame despite the price tag The Steam Frame is certainly not a budget product.
sentences.article_title: Valve's Steam Frame is excellent - but at over £1,000 is VR still too expensive?

sentences.text: But not everyone agrees with the suggestion that VR in general costs too much.
sentences.article_title: Valve's Steam Frame is excellent - but at over £1,000 is VR still too expensive?

sentences.text: "The idea that it's too expensive is one of the biggest misconceptions about VR," UploadVR website editor David Heaney told me.
sentences.article_title: Valve's Steam Frame is excellent - but at over £1,000 is VR still too expensive?

sentences.text: He pointed out while some headsets may be expensive, Meta's Quest 3S budget model costs £320 but has been on sale for £250 several times.
sentences.article_title: Valve's Steam Frame is excellent - but at over £1,000 is VR still too expensive?

sentences.text: "In context, a Nintendo Switch 2 is £420, an Xbox Series S is £430, and a PS5 is £470 - Quest 3S, which is primarily used for gaming, is cheaper than other games consoles," he said.
sentences.article_title: Valve's Steam Frame is excellent - but at over £1,000 is VR still too expensive?

sentences.text: He said the big barrier to more people getting into VR was simply that "we're still in the early days".
sentences.article_title: Valve's Steam Frame is excellent - but at over £1,000 is VR still too expensive?

sentences.text: "You have to see VR in the same timeframe you'd see personal computers in the 1980s," he said.
sentences.article_title: Valve's Steam Frame is excellent - but at over £1,000 is VR still too expensive?

sentences.text: "Even if they had been cheap, which they weren't, they weren't yet good enough for mainstream adoption.
sentences.article_title: Valve's Steam Frame is excellent - but at over £1,000 is VR still too expensive?

sentences.text: "VR is only just getting started, a tech in its 1980s PC era, not something anywhere near maturity." What makes the Steam Frame really stand out is its new tech, including what developers call its "foveated streaming".
sentences.article_title: Valve's Steam Frame is excellent - but at over £1,000 is VR still too expensive?

sentences.text: The tech displays only the exact thing you're looking at in the highest quality, while making things in your peripheral vision less clear.
sentences.article_title: Valve's Steam Frame is excellent - but at over £1,000 is VR still too expensive?

sentences.text: You don't notice the low quality bits because you're not looking at them - saving a massive amount of bandwidth.
sentences.article_title: Valve's Steam Frame is excellent - but at over £1,000 is VR still too expensive?

sentences.text: It means you can stream VR games wirelessly from your PC in high quality without being tethered by a cable, and it works well.
sentences.article_title: Valve's Steam Frame is excellent - but at over £1,000 is VR still too expensive?

sentences.text: And it does this while sending two signals at once - combining your household Wi-Fi with a dongle which plugs into your PC.
sentences.article_title: Valve's Steam Frame is excellent - but at over £1,000 is VR still too expensive?

sentences.text: Valve's Half-Life: Alyx is the most visually stunning game I have played in VR - I've played wireless VR before, but never at this graphical quality when streaming But then again, you need to spend even more money on a decent PC if you want to benefit from that - which doesn't help with concerns about price.
sentences.article_title: Valve's Steam Frame is excellent - but at over £1,000 is VR still too expensive?

sentences.text: Valve says despite it being a VR headset, the Steam Frame is not just for VR games.
sentences.article_title: Valve's Steam Frame is excellent - but at over £1,000 is VR still too expensive?

sentences.text: Selan told me the hope is people will also use it to play their non-VR games too, using the headset as a screen.
sentences.article_title: Valve's Steam Frame is excellent - but at over £1,000 is VR still too expensive?

sentences.text: But it's an interesting thought - and I'd love to be proven wrong.
sentences.article_title: Valve's Steam Frame is excellent - but at over £1,000 is VR still too expensive?

sentences.text: AI has increasingly become part of everyday life over the past decade.
sentences.article_title: What is AI, how does it work and why are some people concerned about it?

sentences.text: The technology takes many forms - from personalising social media feeds to spotting friends in smartphone photos - and accelerating medical breakthroughs.
sentences.article_title: What is AI, how does it work and why are some people concerned about it?

sentences.text: But the rise of chatbots like OpenAI's ChatGPT has prompted concern about the tech's environmental impact, ethical implications and data use.
sentences.article_title: What is AI, how does it work and why are some people concerned about it?

sentences.text: Recent claims that AI could become too powerful and threaten humanity have also triggered calls for slower development and tighter regulation.
sentences.article_title: What is AI, how does it work and why are some people concerned about it?

sentences.text: AI allows computers to process large amounts of data, identify patterns and follow detailed instructions about what to do with that information.
sentences.article_title: What is AI, how does it work and why are some people concerned about it?

sentences.text: Computers cannot think, empathise or reason.
sentences.article_title: What is AI, how does it work and why are some people concerned about it?

sentences.text: The former Mercedes-Benz garage is to be converted into a space for exhibitions, education and community engagement A Turner Prize-winning artist has revealed plans to transform a former car showroom near where he grew up, into a centre for art and learning.

sentences.text: The privately funded project aims to give young people opportunities to experience art after Tyson's own artistic education was shaped by local libraries growing up.
sentences.article_title: Turner Prize winner's new vision for hometown

sentences.article_title: Turner Prize winner's new vision for hometown

sentences.article_title: Turner Prize winner's new vision for hometown

sentences.text: "We're still in the very early stages of the project, but I'm really excited about this beautiful building's potential to become an arts destination, celebrating creativity, especially in the north, and supporting learning and engagement through exhibitions, education, and other resources," he said.

sentences.text: Fannie Masemola will still have to appear in court for the charges to be formally withdrawn South African prosecutors have dropped criminal charges against the country's suspended police chief after concluding there was insufficient evidence to secure a conviction.

sentences.article_title: South Africa prosecutors drop case against suspended police chief

sentences.article_title: South Africa prosecutors drop case against suspended police chief

sentences.text: The Mercator projection is the map widely used across the globe but inaccurately depicts the sizes of countries and continents The UN has just called for the predominant world map to be replaced with one that more accurately reflects the true size of continents such as Africa.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: The "Correct the Map" resolution adopted by the General Assembly aims to fix the discrepancy with the Mercator map, in which the African continent is shown as being of similar size to Greenland - even though it is in reality about 14 times larger.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: The UN adopted a new map, the Equal Earth projection, which better represents the true sizes of landmasses - but comes with problems of its own.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: There have been many prominent attempts over the years to solve the problem of accurately representing the surface of a sphere on a flat rectangle, each with its own benefits and drawbacks.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: The Mercator projection has been around since the 16th Century and was vital for navigating the oceans The now widely used Mercator map was created in 1569 by Flemish cartographer Gerardus Mercator.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: Its main purpose was to help European sailors navigate the oceans, as cartography Professor James Cheshire at University College London explained.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: "He wanted a straight line to be drawn on a map to look like a straight line in reality if you followed a compass bearing," he told the BBC.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: "That was what it was intended to do, and that's what it does brilliantly well." To keep those angles correct on a flat map, Mercator had to stretch the grid lines wider as they moved away from the equator toward the poles.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: His map accommodates for the curvature of the Earth by making countries near the equator seem much smaller than they are and countries nearer the poles appear stretched.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: The distortion is a result of it being impossible to accurately represent the surface of a globe on a two-dimensional chart.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: More than 450 years on, Mercator's creation is still the basis for many of the maps we see in classrooms, on TV and online, including Google Maps.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: But critics of the Mercator map say there is a psychological effect to viewing some places as smaller than they actually are and others as larger, as we instinctively view bigger things as more important.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: For Kenyan geographer Kioko Muendo, this has implicitly downplayed Africa's vast resources, population and investment opportunities.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: "Maps are more than just guides for travellers - they shape how regions are perceived politically and economically," he told the BBC.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: The Equal Earth map aims to represent landmasses' area more fairly The Equal Earth map aims to address this problem with the Mercator projection.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: It was developed by a team of cartographers in 2018 to present the size and shape of landmasses more accurately, and was inspired by the 1963 Robinson projection - a map that shows the entire globe's surface at once.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: As a result, the Equal Earth map was adopted by African Union members in February, before it was adopted by the UN.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: But it sacrifices the straight lines that made the Mercator projection perfect for navigating with - and it cannot be used for measuring the true distance between different places.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: "You can preserve area, or you can preserve shape, or you can preserve distance and direction, but not everything at once perfectly, because otherwise you'd be back to a sphere," Cheshire said.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: The Peters map projection gives a fairer idea of land area but distorts shape The Peters world map was designed by German historian Arno Peters in the early 1970s.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: The rectangular map is based on the projection first described by Scottish cartographer James Gall in 1855.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: The projection sacrifices accuracy of shape in favour of accuracy of scale.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: So, polar regions are squished, while the bits near the equator are stretched.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: This fixes the Greenland-Africa size issue, allowing those who use it to get a sense of the comparative size of different landmasses, all while preserving straight lines of longitude and latitude.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: However, the map severely distorts the shapes of Earth's landmasses, making them all look slightly off.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: Russia, for instance, looks much smaller than it actually is.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: The straight lines on the Peters map also do not represent true constant compass bearings and so are useless for navigation.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: This Mercator projection puts the Americas front and centre instead of Europe and Africa In the same way the apparent size of a landmass can influence its perceived importance, so can its prominence on a map.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: Some cartographers have attempted to orient the map so the south is at the top, to counter the psychological bias that comes from the global south being viewed as less imporant because it's lower down.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: And depending on where you are in the world, which continent is placed in the centre of a map can vary.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: While these alternate maps offer a different perspective on the world to the one we may be familiar with, they don't solve the issue of prominence, but rather simply change the focus of a map.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: The UN flag is centred on the North Pole so no one continent is the primary focus One way of resolving the issue of which landmass is at the centre of a map - and therefore the most prominent - is putting none of them at the centre.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: This is what the map in the UN logo does: the world is centred around the North Pole, with the continents radiating outward from it.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: It's known as an "Azimuthal equidistant projection", placing world regions on a circular map around a focal point.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: The further away from that point on the globe, the bigger the circle.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: On this type of map, all points are at the correct "azimuth" - or horizontal direction - from the centre point.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: But to fit the entire surface of a sphere onto a circle, the map becomes more distorted the further away from the centre it gets.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: On the UN map, for instance, areas near the South Pole appear squished and stretched as what would be a ring of the same circumference as one around the North Pole becomes much larger.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: David Etor's first break came after designing and building a kind of "solar oven" in Nigeria A Nigerian man has shared the story of how he rose up out of "abject poverty" as a child, to become one of the leading UK academics in his field.
sentences.article_title: Nigerian academic on rags to riches: 'Nothing good was supposed to come out of me'

sentences.text: David Etor, 43, who grew up in Nigeria, only learned to read and write aged 12 and was told as a child that "nothing good will come out of you", but is now a lecturer in the School of Electrical, Electronic and Mechanical Engineering at the University of Bristol.
sentences.article_title: Nigerian academic on rags to riches: 'Nothing good was supposed to come out of me'

sentences.text: He told the BBC how his family was so poor growing up that his mum would pretend to cook food in a kitchen they shared with others, "to protect our dignity" in front of neighbours.
sentences.article_title: Nigerian academic on rags to riches: 'Nothing good was supposed to come out of me'

sentences.text: "I didn't see a way out," he said.
sentences.article_title: Nigerian academic on rags to riches: 'Nothing good was supposed to come out of me'

sentences.text: Speaking to John Darvall on BBC Radio Bristol about the publication of his memoir, Etor described growing up in a "compound" with several other families, all sharing a single kitchen, toilet and bathroom.
sentences.article_title: Nigerian academic on rags to riches: 'Nothing good was supposed to come out of me'

sentences.text: "It was a very poor neighbourhood.
sentences.article_title: Nigerian academic on rags to riches: 'Nothing good was supposed to come out of me'

sentences.text: We were particularly very poor that the poor neighbours would refer to us as poor," he said.
sentences.article_title: Nigerian academic on rags to riches: 'Nothing good was supposed to come out of me'

sentences.text: "I do remember that there was a time where my mum would boil water.
sentences.article_title: Nigerian academic on rags to riches: 'Nothing good was supposed to come out of me'

sentences.text: "[She would] go back in and out, lift the lid, stir the water, go back into the room [and] come back as though she was preparing food...
sentences.article_title: Nigerian academic on rags to riches: 'Nothing good was supposed to come out of me'

sentences.text: "She would come back in with that pot of water after a couple of hours and it will be as though she's just finished cooking a meal, but it was just water.
sentences.article_title: Nigerian academic on rags to riches: 'Nothing good was supposed to come out of me'

sentences.text: To solve the problem, he designed and built a kind of "solar oven".
sentences.article_title: Nigerian academic on rags to riches: 'Nothing good was supposed to come out of me'

sentences.text: "It worked incredibly well," he said, which led to an award from the state government and a job.
sentences.article_title: Nigerian academic on rags to riches: 'Nothing good was supposed to come out of me'

sentences.text: That subsequently led him to receive a scholarship to study electrical power at Newcastle University and a PhD at Durham University, before he secured his current job in Bristol.
sentences.article_title: Nigerian academic on rags to riches: 'Nothing good was supposed to come out of me'

sentences.text: Sir Steve Webb, the former MP and Pensions Minister, who got to know Etor through the church in Bristol, called his achievements "remarkable".
sentences.article_title: Nigerian academic on rags to riches: 'Nothing good was supposed to come out of me'

sentences.text: "David's message is very much that people shouldn't be defined by their upbringing or their background," he said.
sentences.article_title: Nigerian academic on rags to riches: 'Nothing good was supposed to come out of me'

sentences.text: "They shouldn't be written off." "I was pinching myself on my way here this morning," Etor added.
sentences.article_title: Nigerian academic on rags to riches: 'Nothing good was supposed to come out of me'
